name: Forging the Heart Grace
summary: The root Charm of the 'Greater Arts of Glamour' -- many noble raksha perform it at the moment of their own birth, literally shaping themselves from the substance of the Wyld and simultaneously creating their own unbreakable Heart Grace, the artifact that houses a creature's Willpower, Nature and volition.
description: This Charm functions as Shape-Forged Servant, but in addition to crafting a creature, it creates an artifact inextricably bound to that creature -- to own one is to own the other. The artifact is the Heart Grace: it is unbreakable, it cannot be stolen except through shaping combat, and it contains a miniature reflection that mimics the creature's activities, letting others observe the creature through it (and, if the Heart Grace is something that opens and closes, use Charms and effects on the creature via the reflection). It also contains the creature's Willpower, giving the creature a Willpower Trait, a Nature, volition and a Heart Trait of 1. Since the Heart Grace cannot be stolen, attuning to it requires first creating, purchasing or winning one; attunement itself takes six scenes of handling and a 1-mote commitment, erasing any previous raksha's attunement, and buys the utter and absolute loyalty and service of the creature associated with that Heart. This loyalty fades if someone else attunes the Heart or if it goes unattuned for a year and a day. Raksha without this Charm were created as property, finding freedom only at the sufferance of their masters or upon their owners' deaths.
cost: 20 motes, 1 gossamer, plus 1 gossamer per mutation point

name: Forging the Cup Grace
summary: Teaches a consenting creature to please others in the manner of the Fair Folk, consuming gossamer to craft it a Cup Grace artifact; anyone attuned to that Cup Grace can reflexively strip it away, reducing the creature's Cup to 0 and inflicting the Curse of Alienation.
description: This Charm consumes a supply of gossamer and creates an artifact with the normal qualities of a finely crafted weapon, suit of armor or tool, in addition to the standard Grace qualities. Raksha and other Essence users can attune to a creature's Cup Grace with six scenes of handling and a 1-mote commitment, erasing any previous raksha's attunement. A character attuned to a creature's Cup Grace can reflexively strip away the creature's comprehensible facade, lowering its Cup to 0 and imposing the Curse of Alienation; breaking or destroying the Cup Grace also inflicts these effects. The raksha who creates a Cup Grace is its initial owner.

name: Forging the Ring Grace
summary: Teaches a consenting creature to see itself as the Fair Folk do, consuming gossamer to craft it a Ring Grace artifact; anyone attuned to that Ring Grace can reflexively strip away the creature's sense of self, reducing its Ring to 0 and inflicting the Curse of Meekness.
description: This Charm consumes a supply of gossamer and creates an artifact with the normal qualities of a finely crafted weapon, suit of armor or tool, in addition to the standard Grace qualities. Raksha and other Essence users can attune to a creature's Ring Grace with six scenes of handling and a 1-mote commitment, erasing any previous raksha's attunement. A character attuned to a creature's Ring Grace can reflexively strip away the creature's sense of self, lowering its Ring to 0 and imposing the Curse of Meekness; breaking or destroying the Ring Grace also inflicts these effects. The raksha who creates a Ring Grace is its initial owner.

name: Forging the Staff Grace
summary: Teaches a consenting creature the ways of Fair Folk diplomacy, consuming gossamer to craft it a Staff Grace artifact; anyone attuned to that Staff Grace can reflexively strip away the creature's understanding of others, reducing its Staff to 0 and inflicting the Curse of Hubris.
description: This Charm consumes a supply of gossamer and creates an artifact with the normal qualities of a finely crafted weapon, suit of armor or tool, in addition to the standard Grace qualities. Raksha and other Essence users can attune to a creature's Staff Grace with six scenes of handling and a 1-mote commitment, erasing any previous raksha's attunement. A character attuned to a creature's Staff Grace can reflexively strip away the creature's understanding of others, lowering its Staff to 0 and imposing the Curse of Hubris; breaking or destroying the Staff Grace also inflicts these effects. The raksha who creates a Staff Grace is its initial owner.

name: Forging the Sword Grace
summary: Makes a consenting creature as terrifying as the raksha herself, consuming gossamer to craft it a Sword Grace artifact that also shields the creature's own Heart Grace from theft by anyone who does not hold the Sword; anyone attuned to the Sword Grace can reflexively strip the creature of its epic mien, reducing its Sword to 0 and inflicting the Curse of Namelessness.
description: This Charm consumes a supply of gossamer and creates an artifact with the normal qualities of a finely crafted weapon, suit of armor or tool, in addition to the standard Grace qualities. Raksha and other Essence users can attune to a creature's Sword Grace with six scenes of handling and a 1-mote commitment, erasing any previous raksha's attunement. A character attuned to a creature's Sword Grace can reflexively strip the creature of its epic mien, lowering its Sword to 0 and imposing the Curse of Namelessness; breaking or destroying the Sword Grace also inflicts these effects. While a Sword Grace exists, its creature's Heart Grace cannot be broken or stolen (whether by shaping combat or mortal theft) by anyone who does not also own the creature's Sword Grace -- raksha sometimes give their Sword Grace to others to safeguard for exactly this reason, though most hesitate to grant such power. The raksha who creates a Sword Grace is its initial owner.

name: Forging the Way Grace
summary: Crafts a Way Grace -- the sixth, exotic shinma Nirupadhika -- as an artifact for a consenting creature, teaching it to tame Nirupadhika and use its shaping actions to speed travel through the Wyld; requires the raksha to already know Forging the Heart Grace.
description: Crafting the Way Grace for a consenting creature, the raksha teaches the target to tame Nirupadhika. This Charm consumes a supply of gossamer and creates an artifact; the artifact has the normal qualities of a finely crafted weapon, suit of armor, or tool, in addition to the standard Grace qualities, and it creates a Way Trait for the creature. Raksha and other Essence users can attune to a creature's Way Grace: this requires six scenes of handling and a 1-mote commitment, which erases any previous raksha's attunement. Characters attuned to a creature's Way Grace can reflexively strip away the creature's connection to Nirupadhika, lowering its Way to 0; the Curse associated with this reduction is left to the Storyteller to determine. Raksha with a Way Grace can use their shaping actions to speed their travel through the Wyld -- a single success on a Dexterity + Sail Way-shaping action moves them one journey through the Wyld.
reviewFlags: The Way is a sixth, exotic shinma outside the five core Graces; its own Curse-on-strip is explicitly left to the Storyteller by the source text, unlike the four core Grace-Forging Charms' fixed Curse pairings.

name: Forging the Arcane Redoubt
summary: Embeds a consenting creature's Heart Grace in an uncapped Demesne, immolating the creature into dormancy and converting the Demesne into a Freehold anchored by an eternal 'bonefire' that others can attune to for reflexive Freehold-wide awareness and automatic shaping successes.
description: The raksha embeds a consenting creature's Heart Grace in the center of an uncapped Demesne. Over the course of a story, it begins to burn until the Heart immolates and becomes a pillar of silver, heatless bonefire; the creature associated with that Heart turns to dust and ash, ceasing to exist until the bonefire dies, at which point the creature returns to life. Building the bonefire turns the Demesne into a Freehold, creating a Cyst or a set of pennants; the Freehold fills with Wyld taint and the Demesne becomes part of the Middlemarches of Rakshastan. The bonefire must be fed dross (a mix of Essence and gossamer) -- 20 motes and 1 gossamer per story -- or it dies and all its effects fail. To attune to a bonefire, a character casts her own Heart into the fire (with the owner's consent if she does not own it herself); for the next six scenes the Heart is vulnerable to theft by normal dice actions or vexation, though reaching into the fire to claim it inflicts one level of aggravated damage. Once the Heart has spent six scenes in the fire, the character is attuned, gaining three benefits: she can 'enflesh' herself within the Freehold as a whole, becoming reflexively aware of everything that transpires there and able to use shaping actions as if present at any waypoint; she receives her Essence in automatic successes on all shaping rolls within the Freehold; and she can reflexively spy on any creature carrying a pennant or Cyst for the Freehold, and can wither or regrow any pennant or Cyst over the course of a story. Raksha outside the Freehold must hold a pennant or Cyst to realize these benefits. Multiple raksha can place their Hearts in the bonefire, dividing the benefits among them and holding power in turn for a duration the bonefire's creator sets (a day, week, month, season, year or story).

name: Forging the Stronghold
summary: Embeds a Sword Grace in a Freehold waypoint, turning it into the Freehold's masculine/martial 'Stronghold' anchor -- protecting against physical invasion, letting the Freehold claim additional waypoints, and granting the attuned character territorial control over the Freehold's physical structure.
description: The raksha embeds a Sword Grace in the spiritual structure of a Freehold waypoint; that Sword Grace and waypoint transform into a 'Stronghold' -- the center and focus of the Freehold's active, aggressive strength, always with masculine or martial symbolism (a fortress, marshalling yard, maypole or mountain peak). Its existence protects the Freehold against physical invasion, and the Freehold gains a Sword Trait (Stronghold Trait) equal to the creature's Sword. A Freehold with a Stronghold can claim possession of additional waypoints, directly controlling a number equal to 10 times its Stronghold Trait. Attuning to a Stronghold requires six scenes of effort and a 1-mote commitment (erasing any previous attunement); the attuning character must have undisputed physical control over the territory, driving out anyone who might object. The attuned character controls the Freehold's physical territory: he can rearrange journeys between waypoints with a difficulty 3 Sword-shaping action (though he cannot isolate a waypoint or reduce the total number of journeys), can enflesh himself in the Freehold's physical structure (gaining awareness of all Sword shaping there, applicable Sword defenses against shaping attacks on the Freehold's waypoints, and the ability to make Sword-shaping actions as if present anywhere in the Freehold). The Stronghold remains the creature's own Sword Grace, and the attuned character can reflexively inflict the Curse of Namelessness on that creature.
prerequisiteText: Forging the Sword Grace, Forging the Arcane Redoubt

name: Forging the Glory
summary: Embeds a Cup Grace in a Freehold waypoint, turning it into the Freehold's radiant 'Glory' anchor -- suffusing the Freehold with beguiling beauty that can compel visitors to linger and submit, and granting the attuned character control over the Freehold's emotional ambience.
description: The raksha embeds a Cup Grace in the spiritual structure of a Freehold waypoint; that Cup Grace and waypoint transform into a 'Glory' -- the center and focus of the Freehold's majesty, radiating a subtle beauty that makes the place magical and wondrous even for mortals tortured within it. The Freehold gains a Cup Trait (Glory Trait) equal to the creature's Cup. A Freehold with a Glory radiates beguilement: characters who relax their mental defenses and accept the Freehold's hospitality must make a Willpower roll (difficulty 1 for raksha, 2 for Creation-born, 3 for Creation-born prisoners) or suffer a beguilement effect compelling them to linger, show no resistance to the raksha, and consent to the raksha's Charms; this effect is a work of glamour with no effect on characters of Wits + Essence 7 or higher. Attuning to a Glory requires an uninterrupted six-scene performance and a 1-mote commitment (erasing any previous attunement); the process fails if the attuning character is driven away or the performance is interrupted. The attuned character controls the Freehold's emotional ambience: she can prevent raksha from regaining Essence naturally there with a difficulty 3 Cup-shaping action, and can enflesh herself in its spiritual structure (gaining awareness of all Cup shaping there, applicable Cup defenses against shaping attacks on the Freehold's waypoints, and the ability to make Cup-shaping actions as if present anywhere in the Freehold). The Glory remains the creature's own Cup Grace, and the attuned character can reflexively inflict the Curse of Alienation on that creature.
prerequisiteText: Forging the Cup Grace, Forging the Arcane Redoubt

name: Forging the Fountainhead
summary: Embeds a Ring Grace in a Freehold waypoint, turning it into the Freehold's self-aware 'Fountainhead' anchor -- a living creature witnessing everything within the Freehold -- and granting the attuned character reflexive perception of the whole Freehold.
description: The raksha embeds a Ring Grace in the spiritual structure of a Freehold waypoint; that Ring Grace and waypoint transform into a 'Fountainhead' -- the center and focus of the Freehold's definition, with feminine or passive symbolism (a well, lake, garden, grotto, mosaic, room-sized mirror or hollow). Its existence gives the Freehold self-awareness and identity, and the Freehold gains a Ring Trait (Fountainhead Trait) equal to the creature's Ring; a Freehold with a Fountainhead is itself a living creature, abstractly and distantly conscious but able to witness everything within it. Attuning to a Fountainhead requires six scenes of effort and a 1-mote commitment (erasing any previous attunement); a majority of the Freehold's Worker raksha must participate, giving their strength to the project. The attuned character defines the Freehold and commands its awareness: she can reflexively sense everything happening anywhere in the Freehold or near any of its pennants or Cysts, can use applicable Ring defenses against shaping attacks on the Freehold's waypoints, and can make Ring-shaping actions as if present anywhere in the Freehold. The Fountainhead remains the creature's own Ring Grace, and the attuned character can reflexively inflict the Curse of Meekness on that creature.
prerequisiteText: Forging the Ring Grace, Forging the Arcane Redoubt

name: Forging the Throne Room
summary: Embeds a Staff Grace in a Freehold waypoint, turning it into the Freehold's 'Throne Room' anchor for court and society -- letting nobles bind themselves in fealty to the Freehold and its lord -- and granting the attuned character control over the Freehold's social fabric.
description: The raksha embeds a Staff Grace in the spiritual structure of a Freehold waypoint; that Staff Grace and waypoint transform into a 'Throne Room' -- a place of court and deliberations, the central focus for the Freehold's society, able to marshal and shape the convictions of others. The Freehold gains a Staff Trait (Throne Room Trait) equal to the creature's Staff. A Freehold's Throne Room allows raksha to bind themselves in fealty to the Freehold and its lord, with the oaths binding the Freehold applying to all such characters until they or the current lord rejects that fealty. Attuning to a Throne Room requires six scenes of effort and a 1-mote commitment (erasing any previous attunement); during the attuning story, the character must meaningfully interact with every noble sworn to the Freehold (gift exchanges, sexual liaisons and plotting together all count, but casual conversation or strictly hostile encounters do not). The attuned character controls the Freehold's social fabric: she can take one oath or adjuration per story on the Freehold's behalf, and can enflesh herself in its social structure (gaining awareness of all Staff shaping there, applicable Staff defenses against shaping attacks on the Freehold's territory, and the ability to make Staff-shaping actions as if present anywhere in the Freehold). The Throne Room remains the creature's own Staff Grace, and the attuned character can reflexively inflict the Curse of Hubris on that creature.
prerequisiteText: Forging the Staff Grace, Forging the Arcane Redoubt

name: Assumption of Elemental Shape
summary: The most common gateway Assumption-type Charm: lets a raksha pass through the shinma Nirakara and exist as a shaped creature within Creation, in one of five elemental variants (Air/Earth/Fire/Water/Wood) each granting a distinct minor elemental resistance or sense.
description: This Charm allows a raksha to pass through the gateway Nirakara and exist as a shaped creature within Creation. This Charm is actually five different Charms, each offering a different benefit: Assumption of Elemental Shape (Air) -- the raksha suffers no ill effects from cold and may walk on snow or ice as if it were solid, stable ground; (Earth) -- the raksha can see clearly in the deepest darkness; (Fire) -- the raksha suffers no ill effects from heat or non-magical flame; (Water) -- the raksha can swim at normal movement rates, breathe water as well as air, and otherwise exist comfortably in an aquatic environment; (Wood) -- the raksha can balance on even the thinnest branch and entirely ignores any natural poison with a single success on a Stamina + Resistance roll. This is an Assumption-type Charm.
reviewFlags: Consolidated the five elemental (Air/Earth/Fire/Water/Wood) variants into one catalog row, matching the inventory's own established precedent for multi-variant single-header Charms.

name: Assumption of Cerements and Bone
summary: A second independent gateway Assumption-type Charm: lets the raksha pass through Nirakara and exist as a shaped creature within the Underworld, treated as dead for all effects while still materially present.
description: This Charm allows a raksha to pass through the gateway Nirakara and exist as a shaped creature within the Underworld. Raksha with this Charm active are material in Creation but, otherwise, are treated as dead for all effects -- they can receive Essence from burnt offerings, Deathlords can feed on them for power, and so forth. This is an Assumption-type Charm.

name: Assumption of the Person's Heart
summary: Lets the raksha pass through Nirakara and exist as a minor Wyld taint on a single visible creature of Creation, optionally sharing the benefits of her mutations and active Charms with that creature (for gossamer) if it consents.
description: This Charm allows a raksha to pass through the gateway Nirakara and exist as a minor Wyld taint on a creature of Creation. The creature must be visible when she uses this Charm. If this is her only active Assumption-type Charm, the raksha exists in Creation as an extension of that creature -- she cannot exist outside its presence, and she involuntarily becomes a dematerialized but manifest spirit when the creature becomes unconscious or someone attempts to forcibly separate her from it. If she has another Assumption-type Charm active, she can leave its presence and does not dematerialize (voluntarily or otherwise) in either circumstance. If the creature consents, this Charm allows the raksha to share the benefits of her mutations and active Charms with it, costing 1 gossamer for each mutation point or gossamer point of Charms shared (for example, spending 1 gossamer to extend Assumption of Elemental Shape (Water) to a shipwrecked sailor); she can withdraw these gifts at any time. This Charm is a work of glamour and cannot taint creatures whose Stamina + Essence exceeds the raksha's Charisma. This is an Assumption-type Charm.

name: Assumption of the Land's Heart
summary: Lets the raksha pass through Nirakara and exist as a subliminal Wyld taint on a hamlet-sized region, sinking her Heart Grace into the land and 'programming' it to trigger works of glamour on specified conditions -- at the cost of losing her own volition and ability to spend Willpower while the Charm lasts.
description: This Charm allows the raksha to pass through the gateway Nirakara and exist as a subliminal Wyld taint on a region of Creation sized to house and feed up to 25 people. The raksha sinks her Heart Grace into the region; mystically separated from her Heart Grace, she cannot spend Willpower and exists without volition, though she can respond to events, defend herself, answer questions and perform repetitive tasks without initiating new courses of action. This Charm lets the raksha 'program' her Heart Grace to trigger works of glamour (such as Fearsome Mien or Beguilement) based on conditions she specifies against any appropriate target within the region; she can access this information consciously with a successful difficulty 5 Intelligence + Lore roll. Discovering the nature of the taint requires a successful difficulty 3 Perception + Occult roll, and tracking it back to the raksha requires a successful difficulty 5 Perception + Occult roll (Charms such as All-Encompassing Sorcerer's Sight allow automatic success). This is an Assumption-type Charm.
reviewFlags: Cross-references Fearsome Mien and Beguilement (both Charms outside this Phase 1b's 19-entry scope) by name only, as illustrative examples; advisory text only, not schema-enforced.

name: Assumption of the City's Heart
summary: Functions as Assumption of the Land's Heart but blankets a city-sized region (up to 1,000 people); if invoked together with Assumption of the Land's Heart, the overlapping central region becomes a place of power where the raksha's Heart can invoke permanent glamours.
description: This Charm functions as Assumption of the Land's Heart, but blankets a larger region -- a place sized to support up to 1,000 people. Fair Folk can invoke this Charm together with Assumption of the Land's Heart; the central region where both overlap becomes a place of power, where the raksha's Heart can invoke permanent glamours as well as works of glamour. This is an Assumption-type Charm.

name: Assumption of the Living Kingdom
summary: Functions as Assumption of the Land's Heart but blankets a small-kingdom-sized region (up to 100,000 people); if invoked together with Assumption of the Land's Heart, the raksha regains the ability to commune with her Heart and take self-directed actions (though still not spend Willpower) while inside the overlapping central region.
description: This Charm functions as Assumption of the Land's Heart, but blankets a much larger region -- a small kingdom, able to support 100,000 people. Fair Folk can invoke this Charm together with Assumption of the Land's Heart; the central region where both overlap becomes a place of power. So long as she remains within that central region, the raksha can commune with her Heart and make decisions; she cannot spend Willpower (although the Heart can), but she can take self-directed actions. This is an Assumption-type Charm.

name: Assumption of the Wyld-Tainted Land
summary: As the Wyld recedes from a region, lets the raksha take a fading Bordermarches area with her through Nirakara, functioning as the larger Assumption-of-the-Land's-Heart-line Charms but additionally infusing the region with enough ambient Wyld energy for the raksha to shape it, at +5 difficulty.
description: As the Wyld recedes from a region, a raksha can take the land with her through the gateway Nirakara. This Charm functions as Assumption of the City's Heart, except the region chosen must be a section of Bordermarches fading into Creation. In addition to the other effects, this Charm creates a powerful tainted land, infused with sufficient ambient Wyld energy for the raksha to shape it, albeit at +5 difficulty. This is an Assumption-type Charm.
reviewFlags: The source's own text calls this Charm's prerequisite line 'Assumption of the Kingdom's Heart,' a name that appears nowhere else in the book; treated as a naming slip for Assumption of the City's Heart (confirmed by both the Prerequisite Charms line and the chapter's own tree diagram) rather than silently corrected -- flagged here per the inventory's own note.

name: Assumption of Dreams and Passion
summary: A worked example of a personalized, non-elemental Assumption-type Charm tree: lets the raksha pass through Nirakara and exist as a shaped creature by filling his spirit with dream-derived emotional Essence, adding his highest feeding Grace in dice to Social rolls that provoke a chosen emotion.
description: This Charm allows a raksha to pass through the gateway Nirakara and exist as a shaped creature within Creation. The raksha fills his spirit with the raw dream-derived Essence of an emotion or passion. This Charm adds the raksha's highest feeding Grace in dice to Social rolls where provoking that emotion is useful. The raksha chooses the emotion in question when invoking this Charm. This is an Assumption-type Charm.
reviewFlags: The source explicitly frames this whole sub-tree as a worked example of the type of personalized non-elemental Assumption-type Charm line a raksha can develop, not the only possible one.

name: Essence-Forging Art
summary: The root Glamour Charm: crafts a serviceable, fine or exceptional item directly from the Wyld's substance, limited in scale and unable to create artifacts or anything usable to benefit shaping actions.
description: The Fair Folk use this art to craft substance from the Wyld. The raksha chooses whether to create a serviceable, fine or exceptional item, and his player rolls Intelligence + Craft (Glamour) as a Ring-shaping action against a difficulty of 1 (serviceable: a normal good-quality item, possibly with a purely cosmetic Wyld quirk at the cost of natural effectiveness), 2 (fine: +1 to one weapon statistic, or +1L/+1B armor soak, with an optional touch of the Wyld such as living eyes or unusual sensory traits) or 3 (exceptional: three +1s split across weapon statistics, or two +1s for armor soak/mobility/fatigue, with aesthetic perfection and Wyld touches). On success, this Charm produces the desired creation. It cannot create artifacts, nor anything large enough for two characters to fight on or in without environmental penalties. Possessions created cannot enter Creation unless the raksha uses an atypical effect such as Elemental Invocation. Tools and weapons crafted with this Charm cannot benefit shaping actions.

name: Principle of Worlds
summary: Carves a serviceable, fine or exceptional territory (home, vehicle or region up to roughly 30 miles across) out of the Wyld.
description: The raksha takes up the crafter's art and carves out landscapes from the Wyld. The raksha chooses whether to create a serviceable, fine or exceptional territory, and her player rolls Intelligence + Craft (Glamour) as a Ring-shaping action against a difficulty of 1 (serviceable: a simple landscape, home or small vehicle), 2 (fine: an unusual tailored landscape, a palatial home, or a large vehicle, with cosmetic touches of the Wyld) or 3 (exceptional: an aesthetically perfect region of significant extent, a great fortress or city, or a First Age-caliber war machine, including complex regional phenomena). On a success, this Charm produces the desired creation. Territories are roughly one journey and one waypoint across, so Creation-born using Charms to traverse them are limited to 30 miles in diameter, often much smaller. Territories cannot enter Creation unless the raksha uses an atypical effect such as Elemental Invocation.

name: Worker's Gift
summary: A repeatable Charm granting bonus gossamer whenever the raksha gains Willpower from fulfilling her nature, purchasable up to her Ring rating with cumulative effects.
description: Through their efforts and dedication, the Workers in the Wyld produce gossamer. This Charm gives the raksha 2 bonus gossamer whenever she gains Willpower from fulfilling her nature. Players can purchase this Charm a number of times equal to the raksha's Ring, and the effects are cumulative.

name: Style-Improving Spirit
summary: Raises the raksha's Style Background by one dot each time it is used, once per story.
description: Tuning her nature in the forge of the Wyld, the raksha gains power over her own definition. Her Style Background improves by one dot each time she uses this Charm, and she can use it once per story.

name: Gossamer-Forging Art
summary: Spends gossamer equal to an item's mundane Resources cost to craft a permanent gossamer wonder over the course of a story, with better statistics than an ordinary exceptional item and no special Charm needed to use it in Creation.
description: Raksha who spend gossamer equal to the mundane Resources cost of the item they wish to create can make truly wondrous works of craft. The raksha's player rolls Intelligence + Craft (Glamour) as a Ring-shaping action. If successful, the raksha must leave the motes committed for a full story as she nurtures the craftwork within her Essence pattern; this Charm creates the desired wonder at the story's end. Gossamer weapons add +1 to accuracy, damage and defense, +2 to their rate, and subtract one dot from their Strength minimum. Gossamer armor has neither fatigue nor mobility penalty. Gossamer tools carry dreams of perfection, adding an automatic success to rolls involving their use; these tool benefits replace the exceptional-item benefits of Essence-Forging Art and never apply to artifacts. This Charm shares Essence-Forging Art's scale limits. Gossamer-forged items are works of permanent glamour, and the raksha can invoke them in Creation without special Charms.

name: Translucent Dream Sheathing Technology
summary: Traps a shaping effort in a permanent web of Essence, will and gossamer, turning a moment's work into a lasting hazardous item or territory (a sleeping castle, a room no one can open) with a scaling difficulty table and an optional Permanence upgrade that lets it enter Creation unaided.
description: The raksha traps a shaping effort in a web of Essence, will and gossamer, transforming it from a moment's work to a permanent possession -- hazardous regions no one ventures into, cabinets no one opens, castles that put every visitor to sleep. This Charm either creates or targets an exceptional item or territory (it can target, but not create, gossamer items). The raksha chooses a serviceable, fine or exceptional effect, and her player rolls Intelligence + Craft (Glamour) as a Ring-shaping action; on success the motes must stay committed for a full story while she finishes the craftwork. A serviceable effect (difficulty 1) can be overcome with a Charm, stunt or Wyld stunt and otherwise imposes the penalties/benefits of an Essence 1 shaping roll on violation or cooperation. A fine effect (difficulty 2) doubles that to a two-die environmental penalty, or can instead produce a one-dot-hazard regional effect. An exceptional effect (difficulty 3) triples it to a three-die environmental penalty, or a two-dot-hazard regional effect. Paying an extra point of difficulty for Permanence lets the result enter Creation without special Charms, treated there as a permanent glamour; without it, the creation needs an atypical effect such as Elemental Invocation to function in Creation at all, even on an item that could otherwise enter normally.

name: Crafter's Arsenal
summary: Forges a permanent shaping weapon over a story, with difficulty set by the Gossamer Background rating needed to buy it and increased for fine or exceptional quality.
description: In the workshops of the Wyld, the raksha forges a shaping weapon. The raksha's player rolls Intelligence + Craft (Glamour) as a Ring-shaping action. The base difficulty of the roll equals the Gossamer Background rating necessary to purchase the item; the difficulty increases by 2 to make a fine shaping weapon and by 4 to make an exceptional one -- so an exceptional curdling dream bow would be a difficulty 8 task. If successful, the raksha must leave the motes committed for a full story as she nurtures the craftwork within her Essence pattern. This Charm creates the desired wonder at the story's end.

name: Glamour
summary: A faster, unstable cousin of the crafting Charms it depends on: creates a servant, item, or territory instantly rather than over a story, but only as a temporary work of glamour that vanishes at the end of its duration and needs a 'seed' of Creation's substance to manifest there at all.
description: The raksha focuses her Essence and wrests gossamer into unstable shapes of glamour, without taking the time to properly accustom the gossamer to shape -- what is made is quickly unmade as its own Wyld nature tears it apart. This Charm creates something from gossamer and Essence, using the rules for Shape-Forged Servant (living creatures), Gossamer-Forging Art (gossamer objects) or Translucent Dream Sheathing Technology (enchanted territories or objects), but differs in that the creation completes instantly, vanishes at the end of the Charm's duration, and is a work of glamour rather than a permanent one (no effect on creatures with Wits + Essence higher than the raksha's Intelligence). In Creation, each creation needs a seed of Creation's substance: servants are transformed out of an insect or simple animal, items out of a mundane item, and regions/homes/vehicles are enchantments laid over existing regions, shelters or transport. This Charm normally lasts one scene per success on the raksha's Intelligence + Craft (Glamour) roll; ignoring the seed requirement and crafting from nothingness instead limits it to one turn per success; using particularly apt seeds (Storyteller's judgment) can extend it to one day per success.
duration: One scene, turn or day per success
prerequisiteText: Translucent Dream Sheathing Technology, Shape-Forged Servant
reviewFlags: Named identically to the broader 'glamour' concept used throughout this book (works of glamour, permanent glamour, Glamour Sorcery); id disambiguated as glamour-charm to avoid collision.

name: Awakened Dream Manufacture
summary: The root of the servant-crafting line: forges a basic, fine or exceptional mindless servant with only the mildest self-awareness, no Willpower, Nature or volition of its own.
description: Most of the servants of the raksha are forged in the same fashion as their tangible possessions; in some cases the tools, foodstuffs and homes of the raksha possess some measure of life. Servants created with this Charm are patterns and dreams with only the mildest self-awareness -- no Willpower Trait, no Nature, no volition -- serving as dictated by their raksha owner. Drawing on the secrets of his own Ring, the raksha forges an awakened dream. He chooses whether to create a basic, fine or exceptional servant, and his player rolls Intelligence + Craft (Glamour) as a Ring-shaping action against a difficulty of 1 (basic: the Traits of a typical citizen, a horse-caliber combat animal, or a mannikin), 2 (fine: an elite soldier, a war dog-caliber combat animal, or a poppet -- the Storyteller can optionally allow other one-dot hazards) or 3 (exceptional: a tyrant lizard-caliber combat animal or a homunculus -- the Storyteller can optionally allow other two-dot hazards). Servants based on human Traits also gain a three-dot Craft or Performance Ability of the raksha's choice.

name: Poppet-Integrating Spirit
summary: Binds a small Wyld creature to the raksha as a familiar, destroying the target's own Heart Grace and increasing the raksha's Familiar Background by one dot per use.
description: The raksha binds a small creature of the Wyld -- a normal or mutated creature with a base form of, at most, Hazard Rating 2 -- to herself. If the creature has a Heart Grace, its Heart Trait cannot exceed 1. This Charm creates a familiar, destroying the target's Heart Grace and binding the creature to the raksha's Heart instead. This Charm increases the raksha's Familiar Background by one dot each time it is used; the raksha's control remains incomplete until she raises her Familiar Background to the point necessary to have the creature. The gossamer cost represents the additional effort needed to bind a mutated familiar. The raksha can bind a creature of her own creation.
cost: 10 motes, 1 experience point, 1 gossamer per mutation point

name: Shape-Forged Servant
summary: Forges a mutation-bearing servant over the course of a story, held for a time outside world and Wyld alike in the gateway Nirakara, gaining one mutation point per gossamer spent.
description: The raksha forges a servant in the gateway Nirakara, holding it away from world and Wyld as she gives it certain characteristics of shape and form. The raksha chooses whether to create a basic, fine or exceptional servant, and her player rolls Intelligence + Craft (Glamour) as a Ring-shaping action against the difficulties listed under Awakened Dream Manufacture. If successful, the raksha must leave the motes committed for a full story as she nurtures the budding creature of shape in her Essence pattern. The completed servant has one mutation point for each gossamer spent, up to the raksha's Craft (Glamour) rating in gossamer. The servant cannot enter Creation without a permanent Assumption-type Charm, unless the raksha uses an atypical effect such as Elemental Invocation. Shape-forged servants are works of permanent glamour.

name: Tainted Creature Command
summary: A Staff-shaping crossover Charm: asserts dominance over lesser creatures of chaos (mutated humans/animals, artificial Wyld beings, and low-Essence common raksha), forcing submission or stripped mutations.
description: Wrapping herself in a shimmering cloak of Wyld energy, the raksha asserts dominance over the lesser creatures of chaos: humans and animals with Wyld mutations; mannikins, poppets, homunculi and other natural beasts of the Wyld; and common raksha whose Essence is less than half the character's own. This Charm forces a successful Willpower roll from such creatures, subtracting any points of mutation they possess, or else they submit to the raksha's authority. This Charm is a work of glamour and does not affect creatures whose Wits + Essence exceeds the character's Charisma; Exalted and other Creation-born Essence channelers are also immune. This is a Staff-shaping Charm.
reviewFlags: Explicitly gated on Staff ('Minimum Staff: 3') despite branching directly off the Ring tree's Shape-Forged Servant and self-declared 'a Staff-shaping Charm' -- a cross-Grace crossover pattern the source uses repeatedly.

name: Monstrous Conceit
summary: A Staff-shaping crossover Charm sitting in the Ring tree's Glamour Charms diagram: forges something directly within a consenting target's mind, functioning as an uncommitted, single-target version of Glamour.
description: The raksha forges something within a consenting target's mind. This Charm functions exactly as Glamour, except that the motes are not committed, the glamour can interact only with the target, and the raksha is treated as having spent a number of gossamer points on the glamour equal to her Essence.
reviewFlags: Explicitly gated on Staff ('Minimum Staff: 4') despite sitting in the Ring tree's Glamour Charms diagram, continuing the cross-Grace crossover pattern this source uses repeatedly.

name: Burden Ghost Glamour
summary: Disincarnates a mechanical burden (encumbrance) from a bound creature, sending it scuttling off into the Wyld in ghostly insectile form, at the cost of consuming an owned Wyld artifact of sufficient level.
description: The raksha disincarnates a burden (in the mechanical sense of an encumbrance) from the creature bound to it; the burden takes on a ghostly insectile form and scuttles off into the Wyld. To power its work, this Charm utterly consumes a Wyld artifact that the raksha owns. Used to lift a character's burden, the artifact must have an Artifact level equal to or above the target's Ring; to lift a waypoint burden in a Freehold or Demesne, the artifact must have a level equal to or greater than the Freehold or Demesne level. This Charm is a work of glamour and does not affect Creation-born characters whose Intelligence + Essence exceeds the raksha's Willpower.
reviewFlags: References Wyld artifacts (pp. 207-208), a mechanic not yet promoted into any catalog -- mentioned here only as plain text in the source, no fabricated cross-reference.

name: Gaping Virtue Mouth
summary: Pries open one of a character's Graces, transforming it into an abstract fanged feeding maw keyed to that Grace's Virtue, granting the character access to the Cup's feeding Charms and natural Essence regeneration in the Wyld or a Freehold, at the cost of treating that Grace as a Major Grace for Charm experience purposes.
description: The raksha interacts with a character and pries open one of that character's Graces, transforming it into a fanged feeding maw that hungers for the emanations of its Virtue. The mouth and teeth exist only in an abstract sense, typically visible only to effects such as All-Encompassing Sorcerer's Sight and in the anima banner of Exalted who acquire a feeding Grace. Characters with a feeding Grace gain access to the feeding Charms of the Cup and can regain Essence naturally in the Wyld or a Freehold; feeding Graces are also treated as Major Graces for the purposes of Charm experience costs. The maximum number of feeding Graces a character can possess equals her Heart rating minus one.
prerequisiteText: Forging the Cup Grace, Forging the Ring Grace, Forging the Staff Grace, Forging the Sword Grace

name: Iron Nightmare Muzzle
summary: A Ring-shaping attack that seals shut an enemy's Virtue mouth instead of dealing normal damage, doubling that Grace's Charm costs until the target can reopen it.
description: The raksha seals over a Grace, closing an enemy's Virtue mouth. The raksha's player makes a Ring-shaping attack against a target no more than one waypoint away. On a success, instead of the normal damage, this Charm seals one of the target's Major Graces so that he can no longer feed from it, doubling the mote cost for all Charms of that Grace until the target can reopen the Virtue maw (for example, with Gaping Virtue Mouth). The Grace remains a feeding Grace -- it is simply not usable.

name: Ecstatic Reproduction Style
summary: A ritual act of communion with the Wyld's mad, amorphous desires that creates a new raksha child, born into servitude with its Heart Grace already in the Charm-user's hand.
description: The raksha performs an act of communion with the mad, amorphous desires and substance of the Wyld. From the delicate shaping of the raksha and the blind primordial urges of chaos, a child is made -- a raksha, prince or servant of the Wyld, born into servitude with the child's Heart Grace in the Charm-user's hand. To use this Charm, the raksha's player rolls Intelligence + Craft (Glamour) as a non-extended action; creating a common raksha is difficulty 5, a heroic commoner difficulty 7, and a noble difficulty 9. On a success, this Charm creates the desired raksha with all five Graces, an appropriate number of them feeding Graces, and the Charm user owns and is attuned to all of them. Botching produces a deformed or suboptimal child -- often an enemy raksha or monster who owns his own Graces.

name: Akshata Sexual Methodology
summary: A Staff-shaping crossover Charm evoking the Staff shinma Nirvikalpa: draws the Essence of two consenting Fair Folk into the raksha and manipulates it to create an oath-bound child, with each parent holding one of the child's Graces.
description: This Charm evokes the aspect of the Staff shinma, Nirvikalpa, letting the raksha draw the Essence of two consenting Fair Folk into himself and manipulate it to create a child. Each parent makes an oath to the other, and the Akshata (the raksha performing the Charm) makes a third oath in the child's name; the child is bound by the Akshata's oath, and the parents' oaths remain sacrosanct only as long as the child exists -- many Wyld treaties are sealed by such oath-children. The parents can contribute motes, gossamer and experience points to the Charm's cost. Each parent holds one of the child's Graces, and the child possesses its own Heart, Ring and Sword. If either parent is raksha, the child is raksha; if either is noble, the child is noble. The children of the unshaped are often prodigies. This is a Staff-shaping Charm.
reviewFlags: Explicitly gated on Staff ('Minimum Staff: 2') despite branching off a Ring-tree Charm and self-declared 'a Staff-shaping Charm' -- the same cross-Grace crossover pattern as Tainted Creature Command and Monstrous Conceit.

name: Great Works of the (Grace)
summary: The Ring's mightiest art of artifact creation: an extended crafting Charm, actually four separate Charms, that forges a fellow raksha's Grace into a permanent artifact of a type keyed to that Grace -- a glamour sorcery spell from a Cup Grace, a Wyld artifact from a Ring Grace, an adjuration from a Staff Grace, or a behemoth from a Sword Grace.
description: This is actually four separate Charms, each forging a specific type of artifact from a specific Grace: Great Works of the Cup forges a glamour sorcery spell from a Cup Grace; Great Works of the Ring forges a Wyld artifact from a Ring Grace; Great Works of the Staff forges an adjuration from a Staff Grace; Great Works of the Sword forges a behemoth from a Sword Grace. A common raksha's Grace becomes a one-dot artifact; noble Graces can become two- or three-dot artifacts. The artifact remains the raksha's own Grace, simply gaining new potence, and characters attuned to it can still reflexively exert the appropriate Curse on the creature. The raksha chooses the artifact's nature, power level and properties, acquires a suitable Grace, and rolls Intelligence + Craft (Glamour) as an extended Ring-shaping action (difficulty 3 for an Artifact 1, 4 for an Artifact 2, 5 for an Artifact 3), leaving the motes committed for a full story per roll. Accumulating 10 successes (Artifact 1), 30 successes (Artifact 2) or 60 successes (Artifact 3) transforms the Grace into the desired artifact as a work of permanent glamour.
reviewFlags: Consolidates the four named variants (Great Works of the Cup/Ring/Staff/Sword) into one catalog row, matching the inventory's own established precedent for multi-variant single-header Charms.

References glamour sorcery, Wyld artifacts, adjurations and behemoths as the artifact types this Charm creates; none of those subsystems (other than Behemoth-Forging Meditation, promoted this phase) has a promoted catalog yet, so those product types stay descriptive text only, not cross-referenced ids.

name: Unshaped (Grace) Transformation
summary: Reshapes an existing artifact born of a Great Works of the (Grace) Charm into a different Storyteller-authorized design of the raksha's choosing -- actually four separate Charms, one per Grace-derived artifact type -- and can also repair damaged artifacts or slain behemoths at reduced difficulty.
description: Molding the Essence and gossamer of an artifact as if it were fine clay, the raksha reshapes existing artifacts to her whims. This is actually four Charms: Unshaped Cup Transformation changes the nature of a glamour sorcery spell; Unshaped Ring Transformation changes the nature of a Wyld artifact; Unshaped Staff Transformation changes the nature of an inactive adjuration; Unshaped Sword Transformation redefines a behemoth. The raksha chooses the artifact's nature, power level and properties, acquires a suitable artifact of the same level, and rolls Intelligence + Craft (Glamour) as an extended Ring-shaping action, with difficulty equal to the artifact's dot rating (this Charm can manipulate Wyld-forged artifacts up to level 5), leaving the motes committed for a full story per roll. Accumulating 3 successes (Artifact 1), 5 (Artifact 2), 10 (Artifact 3), 30 (Artifact 4) or 60 (Artifact 5) reshapes the artifact into a Storyteller-authorized artifact of the raksha's own design. This Charm can also repair damaged artifacts or slain behemoths; if only repairing damage, each roll's difficulty is reduced by one.
reviewFlags: Consolidates the four named variants (Unshaped Cup/Ring/Staff/Sword Transformation) into one catalog row, matching great-works-of-the-grace and the inventory's own established precedent.

name: Behemoth-Forging Meditation
summary: A Sword-crossover capstone that twists a visiting Creation-born creature's nature with mutation points, potentially turning it into a minor behemoth a raksha can attune to and wield as a Sword-shaping weapon.
description: Twisting the nature of a visiting Creation-born creature, the raksha imposes one or more mutations. The raksha's player rolls Intelligence + Craft (Glamour); this Charm changes the target's cosmetic appearance and adds 1 mutation point to the target for every two successes rolled. Essence 1 targets affected by this Charm become minor behemoths -- raksha can attune to them and control them as Sword-shaping weapons. Most have the weapon qualities of basic non-artifact weapons (horrors, mutant warleaders and similar), requiring only a 1-mote attunement to command; mutants with 10 or more points of mutation qualify as one-dot fey beasts. This Charm is a work of glamour and does not affect creatures whose Stamina + Essence exceeds the raksha's Intelligence. Tattooed Lunar Exalted are also immune.

name: Extinction of Desire
summary: The raksha achieves the enlightenment of Nirvishesha by remaking herself as an unbreakable artifact, extinguishing her own volition and self-awareness and delivering her absolute loyalty into the hands of the first raksha to attune to her.
description: The raksha achieves the enlightenment of Nirvishesha and remakes herself as an artifact. Her Heart and Ring Graces turn to dust, and her reflection in her Heart screams in endless agony before fading into foul smoke. This Charm extinguishes the raksha's volition and awareness of self; she can no longer spend Willpower or use the Charms of the Ring. She does not suffer the Curse of Meekness and does not cease to exist -- instead she delivers her will utterly into the hands of the first raksha to attune to her (a 1-mote commitment and six scenes of interaction, functioning only if no other character is attuned). The attuned character can command her as if in possession of her Heart Grace, with absolute loyalty. Raksha affected by this Charm ignore the effects of shaping damage, gain an additional 6L/6B soak against mortal attacks, become unbreakable (automatically converting lethal damage to bashing before soak, unless the attack could damage one of the Five Magical Materials), can be repaired as a damaged three-dot artifact if killed in Creation, and gain the benefits of Mad God Mien.
reviewFlags: Explicitly does not suffer the Curse of Meekness despite extinguishing Ring; see curse-of-meekness for the ordinary broken-Grace rule this Charm overrides.

name: Pox
summary: A repeatable Charm of Shape that manifests a Wyld pox of the player's choice (per the pox lists in Exalted core or Exalted: The Lunars), useful in the design of behemoths.
description: The raksha manifests a Wyld pox (see Exalted core, p. 280, or Exalted: The Lunars, p. 212) chosen at the time of the Charm's purchase. Players can purchase this Charm more than once, choosing a new pox each time.
reviewFlags: The specific pox effect is a fixed table entry chosen by the player at purchase, defined in Exalted core/Exalted: The Lunars rather than in this book -- flagged here rather than transcribed, since this catalog covers Exalted: The Fair Folk's own text only.

name: Affliction
summary: A repeatable Charm of Shape that manifests a Wyld affliction of the player's choice (per the affliction lists in Exalted core or Exalted: The Lunars).
description: The raksha manifests a Wyld affliction (see Exalted core, p. 280, or Exalted: The Lunars, pp. 212-215) chosen at the time of the Charm's purchase. Players can purchase this Charm more than once, choosing a new affliction each time.
reviewFlags: The specific affliction effect is a fixed table entry chosen by the player at purchase, defined in Exalted core/Exalted: The Lunars rather than in this book -- flagged here rather than transcribed.

name: Blight
summary: A repeatable Charm of Shape that manifests a Wyld blight of the player's choice (per the blight lists in Exalted core or Exalted: The Lunars).
description: The raksha manifests a Wyld blight (see Exalted core, pp. 280-281, or Exalted: The Lunars, pp. 215-218) chosen at the time of the Charm's purchase. Players can purchase this Charm more than once, choosing a new blight each time.
reviewFlags: The specific blight effect is a fixed table entry chosen by the player at purchase, defined in Exalted core/Exalted: The Lunars rather than in this book -- flagged here rather than transcribed.

name: Ill-Approving Eyes
summary: The root Charm of the Heart's Dodge Charms tree: a scalable, mote-for-dice bonus to dodging any shaping attack the raksha can see coming, capped by her own shaping Trait plus Dodge.
description: The character's brooding Essence looks down on the game of worlds the Fair Folk play and is unimpressed, declaring with short, sharp gestures of fate the impotence of others' events. For each mote spent, this Charm adds two dice to an attempt to dodge a shaping attack the raksha can anticipate, though the total dice added cannot exceed the raksha's shaping Trait + Dodge. The raksha's player must declare how many motes to spend before the opponent's player rolls the shaping attack.

name: Assertion of a Greater Vision
summary: A cheap, full-power dodge: the raksha denies an anticipated shaping attack as a meaningless background event beneath her own great work of fate, letting her dodge it with her complete shaping Trait + Dodge pool.
description: Setting his name upon local reality, the character denies the world-shaping of others as paltry shadows and dreams -- the events may happen, but they are meaningless background images behind the raksha's own great work of fate. This Charm lets the raksha dodge a single anticipated shaping attack with his full shaping Trait + Dodge dice pool (in Exalted Power Combat, add his Essence to that pool as well). The raksha's player must spend the Charm's cost before the opponent's player makes the attack roll.

name: Sapphire Emptiness Kata
summary: A companion branch to Assertion of a Greater Vision: rather than dodging outright, the raksha simply declares an anticipated shaping attack will not land, raising its difficulty by her Dodge rating.
description: As an opponent works her shaping, the raksha declares, 'This shall not be' -- and it is not. This Charm increases the difficulty to hit the raksha with a single anticipated, dodgeable shaping attack by an amount equal to the raksha's Dodge rating. The raksha's player must invoke this Charm before the opponent's player makes the attack roll.

name: Howling Dream Consumption Prana
summary: The capstone Dodge Charm: for the rest of the story the raksha can reflexively dodge every shaping attack directed at her using her full shaping Trait + Dodge pool, as she opens the mouths of her Graces to devour her enemies' shaped world.
description: The raksha opens the mouths of her Graces, and inside them is the hunger of the void; she eats the world shaped by her enemies. For the remainder of the story, this Charm lets the character reflexively dodge all shaping attacks using her full shaping Trait + Dodge dice pool (in Exalted Power Combat, add her Essence to this pool as well) -- not merely a single anticipated attack, as with its two prerequisite Charms.
prerequisiteText: Assertion of a Greater Vision, Sapphire Emptiness Kata

name: Writhing Ego Evasion
summary: The root Charm of the Heart's Resistance Charms tree: converts spent motes directly into extra soak (via an effective Willpower boost) against a shaping attack, capped by the raksha's own Temperance.
description: Desperate for freedom and the integrity of self, the raksha writhes her way out of the trap of another's shaping. This Charm increases her Willpower by one for every mote spent, purely for the purpose of calculating her soak against that attack. The raksha cannot spend more motes on this Charm in a single use than her Temperance rating.

name: Swallowed Grace Defense
summary: A branch of the Resistance tree that lets the raksha metaphysically swallow her own Graces to seal out an attacker entirely, if the incoming shaping attack's pre-soak damage is weak enough.
description: The raksha metaphysically gulps her Graces into herself, sealing them over with Essence to keep an enemy at bay. She invokes this Charm when someone uses shaping to attack her; if the attacker's pre-soak damage on that attack is less than the raksha's Willpower rating, this Charm lets her ignore the attack entirely.

name: Pyre of Dreams Defense
summary: The other branch of the Resistance tree: a hard damage cap invoked after a shaping attack already hits, scattering the pain into fiery, disastrous images that limit the attack to two damage successes no matter how many dice the attacker rolled.
description: The raksha's pain at a shaping attack scatters images of fire and disaster through the dream. This Charm caps the damage successes of a successful attack that hits the raksha at two, regardless of how many dice the enemy rolled for damage; this cap cannot be further lowered by other Charms or effects. The raksha must invoke this Charm after the attack hits her but before its damage is rolled.

name: Heart-Cutting Style
summary: One of two roots of the Cup Combat Charms tree: after a successful Cup- or Staff-shaping attack, the raksha's artistry wrings extra emotional damage from witnesses by counting her attack's extra successes twice toward damage.
description: The character practices such arts and aesthetics as to rend the witnesses' spirits and make them helpless with emotion. The raksha invokes this Charm after making a successful Cup-shaping or Staff-shaping attack. This Charm lets the raksha count extra successes twice for the purposes of determining damage.

name: Untouchable Performer Technique
summary: Lets the Entertainer raksha parry any single attack using her Cup Grace, rolling Conviction + Performance + shaping weapon defense with her Cup added in extra dice.
description: In the fashion of the Entertainer raksha, the character makes herself sacrosanct. She can parry any one attack with Cup shaping. Her player rolls Conviction + Performance + shaping weapon defense and adds her Cup in extra dice. This Charm cannot generate a defense from nothing -- there must be an initial dice pool for it to add to.

name: Dissonance of Principles
summary: A Cup- or Staff-shaping attack that replaces normal damage with scaling stunning damage, imposing a shaping-dice penalty on the target for three scenes.
description: The raksha's art stuns and disorients his target, scattering patterns of cascading conceptual dissonance through the victim's mind. The raksha spends up to twice his Valor in motes and makes a Cup-shaping or Staff-shaping attack. If he hits, this Charm replaces his shaping damage with stunning damage, doing one level of stunning damage per mote spent; extra successes still add to damage as usual. Stunning damage is soaked only with Temperance. Each success on the damage roll imposes a -1 penalty to the target's shaping dice pools for the next three scenes. Stunning damage is not cumulative -- only the highest result counts, even if this would shorten the duration.

name: Thousand Tiny Hooks Technique
summary: Turns a Cup- or Staff-shaping entanglement attack into a scaling grip that adds the raksha's Essence to both the entanglement's control dice and its damage, and can be invoked even while already entangled.
description: Through her shaping arts, the raksha plants a thousand tiny hooks in the target's soul. The character makes a Cup-shaping or Staff-shaping entanglement attack, receiving the benefits of any readied clinch enhancers. This Charm adds her Essence in dice to the shaping dice pools to inflict, maintain, control and use the entanglement, and also adds her Essence to the damage of her entanglement-based shaping attacks. Although a simple Charm, it can be invoked while entangled; it cannot be placed in a combo with extra-action Charms.

name: Beguilement
summary: A Staff-shaping crossover finale of this branch: makes the raksha's suggestions impossible to resist, functioning as a work of glamour that can manipulate a Creation-born target into almost any request short of direct suicide.
description: The raksha becomes utterly charming, to the point where it is impossible to resist his suggestions. His player rolls Manipulation + Socialize as a Staff-shaping attack, adding the raksha's Charisma in dice to a successful attack's pre-soak damage. Used against creatures with no Staff Grace, this Charm functions as a work of glamour: if the attack succeeds, the target accepts any reasonably phrased suggestion or request as natural, though he will not directly kill himself (he can, however, be manipulated into lethal situations). This Charm does not work on targets whose Wits + Essence or Willpower exceed the raksha's Charisma. This is a Staff-shaping Charm.
reviewFlags: Explicitly gated on Staff ('Minimum Staff: 3') and self-declared 'a Staff-shaping Charm' despite being the terminal leaf of a Cup Combat Charms branch (requiring the Cup Charm Thousand Tiny Hooks Technique) -- the same cross-Grace crossover pattern as Tainted Creature Command/Monstrous Conceit/Akshata Sexual Methodology in the Ring's own trees.

name: Swift Wings of Song
summary: Lets the raksha automatically win shaping initiative over a single opponent by preempting the scene with a whisper of song, a splash of color, or the hint of an idea.
description: Preempting initiative, the raksha sets the stage for her performance with a whisper of song, a splash of color or the hint of an idea. This Charm lets the raksha win shaping initiative automatically over a single opponent. Fair Folk cannot split their dice pool in the same turn they use this Charm. Two characters using this Charm in competition roll for initiative normally.
reviewFlags: The tree diagram on p. 160 (PDF 161) labels this box 'Swift Winds of Song,' conflicting with this Charm's own printed header, 'Swift Wings of Song'; treated as a diagram-art typo rather than a distinct Charm, matching the inventory's own judgment call.

name: Furious Maelstrom Craft
summary: The capstone of the Heart-Cutting Style branch: an extra-action Cup- or Staff-shaping attack whose results apply against a number of enemies equal to twice the raksha's Essence.
description: The raksha crafts a terrible wave of madness and desire that washes out across the local weave of fate. The raksha makes a Cup-shaping or Staff-shaping attack, applying the results against a number of enemies equal to twice her Essence.

name: Subversion and Transformation Artifice
summary: The second root of the Cup Combat Charms tree: crafts a permanent-glamour shaping weapon (chimera, heart thorn, or harness) from Essence and gossamer, letting the raksha divide bonus points among its statistics.
description: The raksha plans and constructs a shaping weapon for her art. This Charm crafts a chimera, a heart thorn, a harness of razored dreams or a harness of twisting words from Essence and gossamer. In addition to the weapon's base qualities, the raksha can divide a number of points equal to her Cup between its speed, accuracy, damage, defense and rate. The creation is a permanent glamour that lasts for one story.

name: Overriding Construct of Fate
summary: An unblockable Cup- or Staff-shaping attack that, on a hit, also knocks the opponent into an adjacent waypoint.
description: The raksha learns to craft patterns of fate seamless enough to seal an opponent out of the ongoing story. The raksha makes a Cup-shaping or Staff-shaping attack. This Charm makes the attack unblockable. In addition, if the raksha hits, this Charm knocks the opponent into an adjacent waypoint.

name: Elusive Object of Desire
summary: The root of the named 'Spirit-Twisting Obsession Style' sub-tree: adds the raksha's Cup in automatic successes to any roll to escape, dodge, or parry an entanglement.
description: Desire is strongest for forbidden fruit, and Entertainers therefore the most elusive of the fey. This Charm adds the raksha's Cup in automatic successes to the roll to escape, dodge or parry an entanglement.

name: Art of Corrosion
summary: Forces a target to channel a praised Virtue on an already-declared action, even one inappropriate to that Virtue, via a contested Cup-shaping roll against the target's Essence.
description: The weave of shaped fate praises the target's Virtues, clothing him in an adamant armor of righteousness that gives every action a numinous glory -- yet even adamant can crumble. The raksha uses this Charm after the target's player declares a shaping or normal action but before the target's player rolls. The player rolls Conviction + Performance in a Cup-shaping attack against a difficulty equal to the target's Essence. On success, this Charm forces the target to channel the praised Virtue on the declared action, even on actions inappropriate to that Virtue. It does not function if the target has no more temporary Willpower or has used all available channels for that Virtue this story.

name: Spirit-Twisting Obsession Stance
summary: A Stance-type Charm naming a single opponent and subtracting the raksha's permanent Essence from that opponent's shaping dice pools, including defensive pools, for as long as the Stance holds.
description: The raksha pours Essence into her Cup Grace, becoming a living symbol of the corruption of self. She names a single opponent, who must be a participant in the current story. This Charm subtracts the raksha's permanent Essence from the targeted opponent's shaping dice pools, including defensive pools. This is a Stance-type Charm; characters cannot use more than one Stance-type Charm at a time.
reviewFlags: This is a Stance-type Charm; characters cannot use more than one Stance-type Charm at a time, per its own mechanics text -- captured here as a narrative note rather than modeled as a schema field, matching this phase's handling of Thousand Tiny Hooks Technique's own Combo-type carve-out.

name: Decaying Principles
summary: A Cup-shaping attack, undodgeable unless the victim channels Temperance, that spreads the corruption of Spirit-Twisting Obsession Stance and erodes the target's held principles.
description: The raksha's corruption spreads. The target finds herself losing the principles she once held dear. The raksha makes a Cup-shaping attack. This Charm makes the attack undodgeable unless the victim channels Temperance into a dodge; it can be parried normally.

name: Twisting Spiral of Collapse
summary: Increases the rate of the raksha's chosen shaping weapon by one as the target's spirit continues to decline; stacks with multiple invocations and works on entanglement weapons.
description: The decline of the target's spirit hastens. This Charm increases the rate of the raksha's chosen shaping weapon by one. Multiple invocations of this Charm stack. Note that this Charm functions on entanglement weapons such as harnesses of razored dreams.

name: Subtle Breath of Ruin
summary: A Cup-shaping attack via Conviction + Larceny that, on a hit, nullifies its own damage but instead raises the difficulty of all the target's shaping actions by the raksha's Essence for the scene.
description: While the raksha's arts distract the target, the target's life -- within the Wyld's false weave of fate -- collapses. The raksha's player rolls Conviction + Larceny as a Cup-shaping attack. If the attack hits, this Charm nullifies the damage of the attack and, instead, increases the difficulty of all the target's shaping actions by the raksha's Essence for the remainder of the scene.

name: Insidious Distraction Technique
summary: Caps the victim's ability to split shaping actions to her Temperance for the scene, and limits dodge/parry actions from a full dodge or parry to Temperance as well.
description: The raksha's presence and practices make concentration difficult for her victim. The raksha uses this Charm at the beginning of the scene. The Charm reduces the victim's ability to split her shaping action: the victim cannot split his shaping action into more actions than his Temperance. The victim receives only his Temperance in dodge or parry actions from a full dodge or full parry.

name: Encouraging Futile Struggle
summary: A Cup-shaping attack that, on success, reduces the target's shaping soak against that single attack by the target's own Willpower.
description: The target attempts to shut out the madness or passion that the raksha invokes and, failing, sinks further into the Entertainer's web. The raksha makes a Cup-shaping attack. If it is successful, this Charm reduces the target's shaping soak against only this attack by the target's Willpower.

name: Brilliant Glinting Lure
summary: Reshapes the raksha into the perfect object of obsession, adding her Performance in dice to her next Cup-shaping action, including reflexive actions such as Art of Corrosion.
description: The raksha reshapes herself into the perfect object of obsession. This Charm adds her Performance in dice to her next Cup-shaping action, including reflexive shaping actions such as Art of Corrosion. The raksha cannot use this Charm to construct a dice pool from nothing.

name: Eulogy for Greatness Lost
summary: The capstone of the Spirit-Twisting Obsession Style tree: a Cup-shaping attack that transforms each post-soak damage die into a success, standing triumphant over the crumbled ruins of the target's life.
description: The raksha stands triumphant over the crumbled ruins of the target's life. The raksha makes a Cup-shaping attack. This Charm transforms each post-soak damage die into a success.
prerequisiteText: Twisting Spiral of Collapse, Insidious Distraction Technique, Brilliant Glinting Lure

name: Flesh-Carved World
summary: One of two roots of the Ring Combat Charms tree: a simple mote-for-dice bonus to a Ring- or Staff-shaping attack, as the raksha unwraps her spirit and imposes its order on the world.
description: The character unwraps her spirit and imposes its order on the world; the law of the self becomes the law of the cosmos. This Charm adds one die to a Ring-shaping or Staff-shaping attack for each mote spent.

name: Shuddering Wyld Inference
summary: Lets the raksha make a blind ranged Ring- or Staff-shaping attack without penalty, useful for attacking individuals on distant waypoints as patterns of Wyld motion ripple against her Essence.
description: The self and the world are one, and patterns of motion in the Wyld are reflected in waves of change rippling and scraping against the raksha's Essence. This Charm lets the raksha make a blind ranged Ring-shaping or Staff-shaping attack without penalty. This Charm is very important for attacking individuals on distant waypoints.

name: Waypoint Knife
summary: Forms an Essence-and-dream knife and, via a successful Intelligence + Craft (Glamour) Ring-shaping attack, swallows an unoccupied waypoint into the Wyld, compressing space so anyone entering it must immediately move on for the rest of the story.
description: The raksha forms a knife of Essence and dream and, with it, cuts a waypoint out of the Wyld. The raksha spends the motes for this Charm and targets an unoccupied waypoint within the maximum range of his shaping weapon, and his player rolls Intelligence + Craft (Glamour) as a Ring-shaping attack. On a success, he swallows that waypoint in the substance of the Wyld; the fabric of space compresses, and for the rest of the story, everyone who enters that waypoint can and must immediately move on to another without spending movement.

name: Mind's Grip Rigor
summary: Forces principle on the Wyld with an iron grip of will, granting either two guaranteed bonus successes on a noncombat Ring- or Staff-shaping action, or six bonus attack successes at half value for damage purposes.
description: The raksha forces principle on the Wyld, her mind locking the bucking, wrestling tides of chaos in an iron grip of will. She can take a Ring-shaping or Staff-shaping action with complete certainty of success. This Charm gives two bonus successes on noncombat Ring-shaping or Staff-shaping actions. It adds six bonus successes to an attack, but halves extra successes for the purposes of computing damage.

name: Creator's Fugue
summary: Grants one extra Ring- or Staff-shaping attack for every 3 motes spent (up to the raksha's permanent Essence in extra attacks), declared on initiative before the attack action.
description: In a mad fugue of creation, the raksha dreams principle upon principle into the shifting void. On his initiative, before taking an attack action, the raksha invokes this Charm and declares the desired number of extra attacks. This Charm gives one extra Ring-shaping or Staff-shaping attack for each 3 motes spent, up to a maximum number of extra attacks equal to the raksha's permanent Essence.

name: Impinging Web of Dream
summary: Weaves the target into a rigid net of shape, granting the raksha a number of extra Ring- or Staff-shaping attacks equal to her Essence, all of which must target the same victim.
description: Weaving the world in an Essence and gossamer-fueled trance, the raksha binds her target in a seething web of shape; the soft and yielding substance of the Wyld becomes a rigid net. This Charm gives the raksha a number of extra Ring-shaping or Staff-shaping attacks equal to her Essence. She must make all of her attacks against the same target.
reviewFlags: The Ring Combat Charms tree diagram on p. 173 labels this Charm 'Impinging Web of Dreams' (plural), but the Charm's own printed header reads 'Impinging Web of Dream' (singular); treated as the same Charm, not a distinct entry, matching the Swift Wings of Song precedent in the Cup Combat Charms tree.

name: Crippling Destiny Burden
summary: A Ring- or Staff-shaping attack from up to one waypoint away that inflicts a stacking -1 environmental penalty on all the target's Sword-shaping actions (per level of damage dealt) until the end of the story.
description: To resist the raw physical power of the martial raksha, Workers and Diplomats often write destinies for the Warriors into the fabric of their created worlds. The burden of such a destiny and its expectations weighs on the target's spirit, distracting him from the victory conditions of the shaping contest. The character makes a Ring-shaping or Staff-shaping attack, from a maximum distance of one waypoint, his player rolling damage normally. For each level of damage this attack inflicts, this Charm inflicts a -1 environmental penalty on all the target's Sword-shaping actions until the end of the story.

name: Wyld-Curdling Attack
summary: The second root of the Ring Combat Charms tree: adds the raksha's Essence in dice to the damage of a successful Ring- or Staff-shaping attack by congealing the Wyld into a horrid trap of form.
description: The raksha's shaping congeals the Wyld, stiffening it into a horrid trap of form. This Charm adds dice equal to the raksha's Essence to the damage of a successful Ring-shaping or Staff-shaping attack.

name: Endless Yawning Void
summary: Surrounds the raksha's Essence in a coruscating aura of time, adding two dice to a Ring- or Staff-shaping action's dice pool and, for attacks, two damage dice per mote spent (up to the raksha's permanent Essence in motes); every raksha within 20 waypoints senses its use.
description: Fair Folk who use this Charm surround their Essence in a coruscating aura of time. Every raksha within 20 waypoints is instantly aware of this Charm's use as the cold touch of causality and rigor rasps against their Hearts. The target finds himself wrapped in layers of dream and the inevitable progression of events, the march of time escorting him inevitably toward his doom or trapping him in an eternity of repetition. This Charm adds two dice to the shaping dice pool for a Ring-shaping or Staff-shaping action. In addition, if that action is a shaping attack, this Charm adds two dice to the damage for each mote spent, and the raksha can spend up to his permanent Essence in motes. This Charm has a minimum cost of 1 mote.

name: Luminous Exhalation
summary: Lets the raksha exhale a fine mist of Essence that Ring-shaping weapons can use as gossamer, allowing a single Ring- or Staff-shaping attack without the need for gossamer ammunition per use.
description: The weakness of ranged Ring-shaping attacks is their dependence on ammunition. This Charm lets the raksha exhale a fine mist of Essence that Ring-shaping weapons can use as gossamer. Each use allows a single Ring-shaping or Staff-shaping attack without the need for gossamer ammunition.

name: Twisting Serpent Shape
summary: Lets the raksha make a single Ring- or Staff-shaping attack without gossamer ammunition, using her readied ranged shaping weapon's accuracy but a base damage of Perception + 10 at a fixed 10-waypoint range.
description: The raksha curls the local weave of fate in on itself, building a twisting world of circular reasoning and self-justifying propositions that, with the raw writhing vitality of a living thing, shapes itself to ensure its continued existence. The Essence of the raksha's shaping weapon and the Essence of the world are mirrors of one another. This Charm allows the raksha to make a single Ring-shaping or Staff-shaping attack without gossamer ammunition. This attack uses the accuracy of his readied shaping weapon, which must have a nonzero waypoint range. The base damage of the attack is the raksha's Perception + 10, and the range of the attack is 10 waypoints' distance.

name: Gaping Wound Lens
summary: Rips open the raksha's Essence pattern to form a permanent lens usable for either Ring- or Staff-shaping ranged attacks, with accuracy/rate equal to Essence, 10-waypoint range, and no Perception/Charisma damage cap.
description: The raksha rips open his Essence pattern, using the bleeding hollow this forms as a lens. This lens has accuracy and rate equal to the raksha's permanent Essence and a range of 10 waypoints. The raksha can use his gaping wound lens to make either Ring-shaping or Staff-shaping attacks; these have a base damage of Perception + Essence or Charisma + Essence, respectively. This lens has no Perception or Charisma maximum.

name: Pounding Dream Harmony
summary: Sets forth many shaping principles in subtle harmony: on a successful Ring- or Staff-shaping attack, lets the raksha ignore up to one point of the enemy's soak per mote spent.
description: The raksha speaks the law of the world not in words, but in chorus. She sets forth not one, but many principles in subtle harmony and arrangement. The raksha spends the motes for this Charm and makes a Ring-shaping or Staff-shaping attack.
