If this attack succeeds, this Charm lets her ignore up to one point of the enemy's soak for each mote spent.

name: Sorrowful Firmament Resonance
summary: Sings Nirvishesha's Sayujya aspect to sink the raksha's will into the Wyld's substrata: an undodgeable (though parriable) Ring- or Staff-shaping attack against a target within three waypoints, its effect felt by every local waypoint and raksha's spirit within 10 waypoints.
description: Singing the sonorous lament of Nirvishesha's Sayujya aspect, the raksha sinks her will into the substrata of the Wyld. She makes a Ring-shaping or Staff-shaping attack against a target no more than three waypoints away. There is no escape from this attack -- parrying is possible with stunts and Charms, but dodging is impossible. Every local waypoint and every raksha's spirit, within a 10 waypoints' distance, shivers with her song.

name: Undetectable Lie
summary: A Staff-shaping crossover finale of the Ring Combat Charms tree: defines the law of the world in such compelling terms that even Creation-born targets accept one statement as absolute truth, converting post-soak damage into automatic successes.
description: The raksha defines the law of the world in such compelling terms that not even the Creation-born can refuse belief. Her player rolls Manipulation + Socialize as a Staff-shaping attack, converting the post-soak damage dice into automatic successes. Used against creatures with no Staff Grace, this Charm functions as a work of glamour: the target accepts any one statement of the raksha's as absolute truth. It takes one scene before the target is receptive to contradictory evidence, and even then most targets remember it as a distortion in the world rather than their senses. This power does not work on targets whose Wits + Essence is greater than the raksha's Manipulation. This is a Staff-shaping Charm.
reviewFlags: Explicitly gated on Minimum Staff (not Ring) and self-declared 'a Staff-shaping Charm' despite terminating a Ring Combat Charms branch -- the same cross-Grace crossover pattern already seen in the Ring's own Tainted Creature Command/Monstrous Conceit/Akshata Sexual Methodology and the Cup tree's Beguilement.

name: These Dreams Are Clay
summary: The last Charm of the Ring Combat Charms tree: massages the unformed Wyld into 1 unstable gossamer that fades at the end of the next scene, usable only in the Middlemarches or deeper Wyld regions.
description: The craft of the Workers brings forth gossamer from the Wyld. Massaging the unformed shapeless world with his hands, a raksha in the Middlemarches or deeper regions of the Wyld can create 1 gossamer from Essence. Gossamer created by this Charm is unstable and fades at the end of the next scene.

name: Wyld Communion
summary: The root Charm of the All-Consuming God-Monster Style: meditating on the Wyld's own birth-principles, the raksha adds one extra die to all of her stunts while in the Wyld.
description: The raksha meditates on the Wyld, dredging forth and harmonizing with the strange Essence of the principles that gave the Wyld birth. This Charm improves all her stunts by one die (for example, a one-die stunt would add two dice to her pool). This functions only in the Wyld.

name: Spirit-Flaying Meditation
summary: Strives for harmony with a greater principle by cutting a Charm or Trait out of the raksha's own soul, at no other compensation.
description: Striving for harmony with a greater principle, the raksha cuts a Charm or Trait out of her own soul. This Charm removes one of the raksha's Charms from the character sheet or lowers one of her own Traits by one. Raksha who lose a Charm also lose any permanent mutations gained through purchase of that Charm. The raksha receives no other compensation for the loss.

name: Being-Nonbeing Approach
summary: Elides the raksha from the shaped world into undirected immanent power, raising the difficulty of targeting her with shaping actions and boosting her Stealth against non-Essence-sighted observers.
description: The raksha elides herself from the shaped world, becoming undirected immanent power inherent in the nature of existence. The raksha's player rolls Intelligence + Martial Arts. On a success, this Charm increases the difficulty of targeting her with shaping actions by one. The Creation-born can still make out her shadowy form in some specific location within the world, but successful use of this Charm also adds her highest feeding Virtue in dice to normal Stealth dice actions unless those attempting to see her have All-Encompassing Sorcerer's Sight or some other form of Essence sense.

name: All-Consuming God-Monster Stance
summary: The style's central Stance-type Charm: transforms the raksha's Essence into a purchasable 'God-Monster Body' that grants a menu of special gifts (three on first purchase, two per subsequent purchase), incompatible with Assumption-type Charms unless the raksha also takes the Calling Upon the Dragon's Ire gift.
description: The raksha strives for transcendence, making herself a channel for the deepest madness of the Wyld and hammering herself into a shape defined by imperatives that predate reason and existence. This Charm transforms the raksha's Essence, giving her what the Fair Folk call a 'God-Monster Body.' The first purchase grants three gifts, chosen immediately; each subsequent purchase grants two more gifts. Gifts exist only while this Charm is in force, many have prerequisite gifts that must be taken first, and no gift can be taken more than once. Raksha can purchase this Charm only once, but unshaped can buy it a number of times equal to half their Essence. Sample gifts (a non-exhaustive menu per the sourcebook's own sidebar) include: Advaita Harmony (three extra Virtue dots split freely, and Virtues can be violated without spending Willpower, while in God-Monster form); Calling Upon the Dragon's Ire (lets an Assumption-type Charm and this Charm run simultaneously -- required for any raksha with an Assumption-type mutation who wants this Stance); Chain-Defying Art (heals one level of shaping damage per scene), upgradable to Untouchable Infinite Spirit (heals all of one chosen shaping damage track plus one point of each other type per scene, replacing Chain-Defying Art's benefit); Fearsome Radiance (low-Valor attackers/defenders suffer +1 difficulty against the raksha), extendable to World-Devourer's Shadow (low-Essence characters' players must pass a difficulty-1 Valor roll once per scene even to attempt attacking the raksha, on top of the Fearsome Radiance penalty); Graces of the Wyld (immunity to the Curses of Alienation, Hubris, Namelessness and Meekness while in God-Monster form); Heart-Stopping Numinous Power (+2 effective Essence in God-Monster form); Lumbering Feet of God (travel three waypoints per scene or sprint six); Terrible Shaping Suasion (+2 dice on all shaping rolls in God-Monster form); and Unshapeable Transcendent Essence (adds Essence to shaping soak), extendable to Miasma of Principle (also adds Essence to natural lethal and bashing soak, cumulative with Unshapeable Transcendent Essence). This Charm is specifically incompatible with Assumption-type Charms unless the raksha takes Calling Upon the Dragon's Ire. This is a Stance-type Charm; characters cannot use more than one Stance-type Charm at a time.
reviewFlags: This is a Stance-type Charm; characters cannot use more than one Stance-type Charm at a time (the same unmodeled mechanic flagged for Spirit-Twisting Obsession Stance in the Cup Combat Charms tree -- no schema field tracks Stance-type exclusivity). Also explicitly incompatible with Assumption-type Charms unless the raksha also takes the Calling Upon the Dragon's Ire gift. The 'description' field paraphrases and condenses the sourcebook's own 'Sample God-Monster Body Gifts' sidebar rather than reproducing every gift verbatim, per the inventory's own note.

name: Nature-Eliminating Knife
summary: Utterly destroys one of the raksha's own Graces, wherever it dwells, permanently adding the 'Graces of the Wyld' gift (or any other gift of her choice, if she already has it) to her God-Monster Body.
description: This Charm utterly destroys one of its user's own Graces, no matter in whose hands it dwells. Invoking this Charm permanently adds the 'Graces of the Wyld' gift to the raksha's God-Monster Body or, if the raksha's God-Monster Body already has this gift, adds any other gift of the raksha's choice.

name: Chimera Exultation
summary: The style's capstone: assuming a God-Monster Body, the raksha destroys her own Heart Grace and vanishes in a flare of pearlescent light, utterly annihilating herself as a Storyteller-controlled plot device.
description: Assuming a God-Monster Body, the raksha destroys her Heart Grace and vanishes in a flare of pearlescent light. This Charm utterly destroys the raksha who uses it, driving the radiance of the raksha's will and desire into the substrata of the Wyld. This Charm is a plot device, having such limited or limitless effects as the Storyteller desires.

name: Furiously Stalling Destiny
summary: The root Charm of the Staff's 'Laughing Monster Style' Charm tree: a diplomatic counterattack that lets the raksha protest a shaping contest by countering with his full Manipulation + Occult pool the moment an opponent attacks him.
description: The raksha uses diplomatic techniques to protest the shaping contest. This Charm lets him issue a Staff-shaping counterattack with his full Manipulation + Occult dice pool against an opponent who has just used a shaping attack against him; the counterattack resolves after the opponent's attack roll but before that attack's damage effects are applied. He can only make one such counterattack per triggering attack, and he cannot use this Charm's counterattack to answer another counterattack. Supplemental Charms placed in a Combo with this Charm enhance the counterattack.

name: Deeper Into Trouble Technique
summary: Drives a shaping-attack target into fury, punishing him with a Willpower drain if his very next shaping attack targets someone other than the raksha.
description: The raksha drives an opponent into fury. The raksha's player rolls Manipulation + Occult as a Staff-shaping attack; on a hit, damage applies normally, but the attack also infuriates the target, provoking him to lash out at the raksha specifically. If the target's next shaping attack action targets anyone other than the raksha, this Charm drains one of that target's temporary Willpower points.

name: Laughing Monster Stance
summary: The central Stance-type Charm of the Laughing Monster Style tree: lets the raksha reflexively redirect a missed shaping attack against any target of her choice, including the original attacker, for a full story.
description: The raksha pours Essence into her Staff Grace, becoming the dweller in the between -- the laughing monster who dances through the cracks in society and twists oaths against their holders, confounding her enemies and turning their own efforts against them. If a shaping attack misses her while this Charm is active, she can reflexively spend 1 Willpower to redirect it against any target of her choice, including the original attacker; the attack is rerolled against the new target as though it had been aimed there from the start. This is a Stance-type Charm, and a character cannot have more than one Stance-type Charm active at a time.
reviewFlags: This is a Stance-type Charm; a character cannot have more than one Stance-type Charm active at a time (the same unmodeled mechanic already flagged for Spirit-Twisting Obsession Stance and All-Consuming God-Monster Stance -- no schema field tracks Stance-type exclusivity).

name: Unitary Being Forge
summary: One of three Charms branching from Laughing Monster Stance: turns an opponent's existing shaping wounds into bonus damage dice for the raksha's own attack.
description: The raksha exploits an awkward situation for diplomatic advantage. His player rolls Manipulation + Occult as a Staff-shaping attack; on a success, this Charm adds one damage die for every point of Sword, Ring or Cup damage the opponent is currently suffering.

name: Inauspicious Moment for Attack
summary: A second Charm branching from Laughing Monster Stance: a scene-opening initiative attack that can lock a badly-timed opponent out of taking any shaping action that scene at all.
description: With the arts of distraction and omen, the laughing monster slows the enemy's advance. The raksha must use this Charm at the very beginning of the scene; it reduces a chosen opponent's shaping initiative by twice the raksha's Essence. If this drops the opponent's shaping initiative below 1, that opponent cannot take a shaping action at all for the rest of the scene, though he can still activate reflexive effects.

name: Thieves Fall Out
summary: The third Charm branching from Laughing Monster Stance: sets two named targets against each other, inflicting recurring unblockable Staff damage on the first whenever both occupy the same or adjacent waypoints.
description: The raksha encourages enmity between two foes. She names two targets, and her player rolls Manipulation + Occult as a shaping action against a difficulty equal to the first target's Essence. On a success, this Charm inflicts one level of unblockable, undodgeable Staff damage on the first target for every scene in which the two named targets occupy the same waypoint or adjacent waypoints.

name: Shuffling the Pieces
summary: Builds on Unitary Being Forge: instead of dealing her own damage, the raksha redistributes up to 10 levels of a target's existing Sword/Ring/Cup damage as healing, dumping an equal amount onto the target's Staff Grace instead.
description: The raksha's words revise the world, so that the pounding march of armies, the stringent laws of the world and the harmonious strains of an Entertainer's vision become nothing more than diplomatic tools. Her player rolls Manipulation + Occult as a Staff-shaping attack; on a success, instead of applying her normal damage, she heals up to 10 total levels of the target's Sword, Ring and Cup damage (divided among those tracks however she chooses) and immediately inflicts that same total amount of damage on the target's Staff Grace. This lets the raksha use the Charm to 'heal' allies just as readily as to further damage enemies.

name: Subtle Hammer
summary: Builds on Inauspicious Moment for Attack: a nearly undefendable Staff-shaping attack that the opponent cannot parry or dodge without Charms, and whose extra successes count double toward damage.
description: The Diplomat's work is subtle, and the opponent does not notice its danger until too late. The raksha makes a Staff-shaping attack; the opponent cannot parry or dodge it without the use of Charms, and the raksha doubles her extra successes for the purposes of determining damage.

name: Poisoned Whispers
summary: Builds on Thieves Fall Out: if a poisoned target attacks the raksha and misses, she can reflexively redirect that failed attack against any target of her choosing at no Willpower cost.
description: The raksha poisons and twists the mind of a target. If that target attacks the raksha and misses during the scene this Charm is active, she can reflexively redirect the failed attack against any target of her choice -- including the original attacker -- without needing to spend a Willpower point to do so (unlike the similar redirection granted by Laughing Monster Stance).

name: Dancing Wind Monster Transformation
summary: The capstone Charm of the Laughing Monster Style tree: the raksha fades into invisible, laughing wind, leaving only the echo of her spiteful words as her enemies turn on each other, and gains a large automatic bonus on all her shaping dodges for the story.
description: The raksha fades into the wind, laughing, invisible, leaving nothing but the echo of her spiteful words; bereft, her enemies must turn on one another. This Charm adds the raksha's Essence rating as automatic successes to all of her shaping dodge actions for the rest of the story.
prerequisiteText: Shuffling the Pieces, Subtle Hammer, Poisoned Whispers

name: Oath Gossamer
summary: The root Charm of the Staff's separate 'Society-Forging Charms' tree, which raksha use to literally construct their society: binds the raksha to a consenting partner in a named relationship that generates gossamer for as long as it is actively pursued, at the cost of shattering the raksha's Staff Grace if she ends it permanently.
description: The raksha binds himself to a consenting raksha in a gossamer-producing relationship, which can be any relationship the two agree to -- from true love to rivalry to bitterest hate. This Charm grants him 1 bonus gossamer in every story during which he actively pursues the named relationship. If he ever brings that relationship to a permanent end, this Charm instead breaks his Staff Grace and scatters its pieces.

name: Eight-Corner Ring Binding
summary: Scales Oath Gossamer up from a pair to a group of up to eight raksha, each declaring a relationship with every other member; breaking any one relationship shatters that member's Staff Grace and hands out its pieces to the rest of the ring.
description: This Charm, the basic unit of pragmatic raksha alliance, binds a group of up to eight raksha into a ring; each member names a desired relationship with each of the others, exactly as with Oath Gossamer. At the end of every story, each raksha in the ring receives 1 bonus gossamer per relationship she actively pursued that story. If any raksha in the binding permanently ends one of her relationships, her Staff Grace shatters, and each of the other raksha in the ring receives one piece of it. Members can revise their declared relationships, but must announce the change a full story in advance.

name: God-Humbling Victory Sword
summary: The root Sword Combat Charm: calls Nishkriya into the aspect of the raksha's Sword and fills the world with portents of victory, adding bonus dice to a single Sword- or Staff-shaping attack.
description: The raksha calls Nishkriya into the aspect of her Sword and fills the world with portents of her victory. This Charm adds one or more dice to a single Sword-shaping or Staff-shaping attack.

name: Scourging Wind Raid
summary: A lightning raid that lets the raksha steal a named possession from a target as part of a Sword- or Staff-shaping attack, at increased difficulty.
description: In a lightning raid, the raksha steals the wealth of her foe. The raksha spends the motes for this Charm, names one of the target's possessions, and makes a Sword-shaping or Staff-shaping attack at +2 difficulty. If successful, this Charm co-opts ownership of that possession in addition to inflicting normal damage. The Charm cannot steal Graces, artifacts or Hearthstones, but it can steal shaping weapons, including readied weapons.

name: Dream Sacrificing Method
summary: Lets the raksha negate incoming Sword-shaping attack damage by sacrificing gossamer equal to the damage successes, transferring that gossamer to the attacker.
description: Even the living deities of battle must choose their sacrifices. The raksha invokes this Charm after an enemy rolls damage for a Sword-shaping attack. The raksha can negate this damage by sacrificing gossamer equal to the damage successes; this Charm negates the damage but transfers the gossamer into the attacker's hands.

name: Unparalleled Terror Technique
summary: Englamours an ordinary Sword- or Staff-shaping attack with the touch of nightmare, doubling extra successes for damage purposes if the attack succeeds.
description: The raksha's Sword hungers for the fear of her foe. Her shaping englamours an ordinary blow with the touch of nightmare. This Charm augments a single Sword-shaping or Staff-shaping attack; if the attack succeeds, the raksha counts extra successes twice for purposes of dealing damage.

name: Pincer of Transcendent Time and Fate
summary: Takes on the aspect of Kala and Dharma, the paired weapons of Nishkriya that strike as one, letting the raksha launch two Sword- or Staff-shaping attacks at full dice pool using a single shaping action.
description: The raksha's Sword takes on the aspect of Kala and Dharma, the paired weapons of Nishkriya that strike as one. This Charm uses the raksha's shaping action to launch two Sword-shaping or two Staff-shaping attacks at her full dice pool.

name: Endless Armies of the Storm
summary: Calls an endless host driven forth by flute and drum, letting the raksha make additional Sword- or Staff-shaping attacks (one per 3 motes spent, up to her permanent Essence) alongside her normal shaping action.
description: The raksha opens her spirit with Nishkriya, the Sword, and calls an endless host. Driven forth by the sound of flute and drum, the limitless armies of the Wyld march. In addition to the raksha's normal shaping action, this Charm lets her make one Sword-shaping or Staff-shaping attack for each 3 motes of Essence spent, up to a limit of her permanent Essence.
prerequisiteText: Pincer of Transcendent Time and Fate

name: Host-Summoning Glory of Command
summary: The second independent root of the Sword Combat Charms tree: the raksha wears a visible mantle of martial greatness, letting her draw armies, monsters and champions into an ongoing story and instantly ready a Sword- or Staff-shaping weapon before her initiative.
description: The raksha wears the mantle of greatness, visibly displaying her terrible aptitude for war. She can draw her armies, monsters and champions into an ongoing story without further explanation of their presence. This Charm instantly readies a Sword-shaping or Staff-shaping weapon; the raksha can use this Charm before her initiative.

name: Sundering the Gates of Death
summary: Lets the raksha instantly re-ready a slain or scattered Sword- or Staff-shaping weapon (army, behemoth or even her own body) before her initiative, though it cannot restore the permanently slain.
description: The raksha commands death, and it is not her master. If her army is slain or scattered, she can call it back; if her behemoth is slain or driven away, she can restore it; even should an enemy shatter her bones and leave her bloody and broken on the field, she can restore herself and continue the fight. This Charm instantly readies a Sword-shaping or Staff-shaping weapon, even if that weapon has been slain or otherwise driven from the battle; the raksha can use it before her initiative. This Charm cannot restore the permanently slain.

name: Transient Work of Flesh and Bone
summary: Shapes a behemoth or a host of warriors out of gossamer as a Sword-shaping weapon, built from the raksha's own Sword Grace and Willpower, though the work of glamour cannot affect Creation-born residents above a Wits + Essence threshold.
description: The raksha shapes a behemoth or a host of warriors from gossamer. This Charm forms a shaping weapon of the Sword; the player divides twice the raksha's Sword Grace between the weapon's speed, accuracy, damage and defense, and its rate equals the raksha's permanent Willpower. The weapon formed is a monster (a fey beast) or a small army (a unit of 500 extras using the elite troop Traits from Exalted core, p. 278). Either way the result is a work of glamour: it cannot attack, defend or soak against residents of Creation whose Wits + Essence exceeds the raksha's Valor.

name: Scattering the Foe
summary: The root of two further Sword Combat Charm branches: takes on the aspect of Shikhari, the hammer that scatters armies, letting the raksha buy dice to block a Sword- or Staff-shaping attack even from nothing, provided she is aware of it.
description: The raksha's sword takes on the aspect of Shikhari, the hammer that scatters armies. An enemy attack shatters against the raksha's battle prowess. This Charm allows the raksha to buy dice for blocking Sword or Staff attacks -- she can improve a normal shaping parry or build a shaping dice pool from nothing. She must be aware of the attack.

name: Radiance of the Invincible Warrior
summary: Binds back fear and death from the raksha's assembled forces, letting her parry any one Sword or Staff attack with her full dice pool provided she is aware of it.
description: The raksha's Sword Grace binds back fear and death, so that they come only grudgingly to her assembled forces. This Charm lets the raksha parry any one Sword or Staff attack with her full dice pool. She must be aware of the attack.

name: Waypoint-Sealing Technique
summary: Takes up the Raghava aspect of the Sword's defensive posture, letting the raksha seal an opponent out of a waypoint she occupies or controls with an undodgeable Sword-shaping attack.
description: Taking up the powerful defensive position typified by the Raghava aspect of the Sword, the raksha seals an opponent out of a waypoint. The raksha uses this Charm as an opponent enters a waypoint she occupies or controls, and her player rolls Dexterity + Melee as an undodgeable Sword-shaping attack. If she achieves even one success, the opponent cannot enter the waypoint this scene and loses that portion of her movement.
reviewFlags: The 'Sword Combat Charms 2' tree diagram labels this Charm 'Waypoint Sealing Stance,' but its own printed header and stat block both read 'Waypoint-Sealing Technique' with Type: Reflexive (not a Stance-type Charm); treated as a diagram/header naming mismatch, matching the Swift Wings of Song/Impinging Web of Dream precedent.

name: Unconquerable Truth
summary: Invokes truths of the raksha that no weaving of fate can master, letting her parry any one Sword- or Staff-shaping attack with her full dice pool plus six bonus successes, even against a normally unblockable attack.
description: There are some warriors who cannot be defeated; there are some generals whom no mind can outmaneuver; there are truths of the raksha that no paltry weaving of fate and story can master. This Charm lets the raksha parry any one Sword- or Staff-shaping attack with her full dice pool, adding six bonus successes, even if that attack is normally unblockable.

name: Rarefied Air of Inevitable Victory
summary: The raksha masters the destiny of war for a full story, reflexively parrying any Sword or Staff attack against her with her full dice pool even without being aware of it.
description: The raksha masters the destiny of war. Cast itself at her though it might, the enemy cannot keep her forces down -- they endure the most horrific assaults, they regroup after the most terrible of blows, and not all the greatest nightmares of the Wyld can keep the raksha from her appointed goal. This Charm allows the raksha to reflexively parry any Sword or Staff attack against her with her full dice pool; she need not be aware of the attack. This paramount skill lasts until the end of the story.
prerequisiteText: Sundering the Gates of Death, Radiance of the Invincible Warrior

name: Defining the Parameters of Battle
summary: Writes the raksha's own invincibility into the pattern of the world for a full story, letting her spend gossamer to parry any Sword-, Staff-, or even mortal attack with her full dice pool plus six bonus successes.
description: The raksha writes her own invincibility into the pattern of the world. While this glamour endures, no Sword shaping can defy the essential truths of her nature: she can spend 1 gossamer to parry any one Sword- or Staff-shaping attack with her full dice pool plus six bonus successes, even if that attack is normally unblockable. In addition, she can spend 1 gossamer to parry any mortal attack with her full Dexterity + Melee pool plus six bonus successes, even if normally unblockable; this defense is a work of glamour and does not function against mortals with Wits + Essence greater than the raksha's Stamina.
prerequisiteText: Unconquerable Truth, Rarefied Air of Inevitable Victory

name: All-Inclusive Nightmare Defense
summary: Unleashes fear and doubt on the raksha's enemies after a successful parry, disarming the attacker's Sword- or Staff-shaping weapon from readiness by routing or killing the forces behind it.
description: The raksha unleashes fear and doubt upon her enemies, dispersing and driving back the weapons of the Sword. To use this Charm, she must successfully parry a Sword attack and receive extra successes equal to or exceeding the attacker's permanent Essence. This Charm removes the enemy's Sword-shaping or Staff-shaping weapon from readiness, normally by routing or killing the enemy's forces.

name: Tension-Building Warrior's Advance
summary: Takes on the aspect of the supreme divine emissary of death, supplementing a Sword or Staff attack by raising the difficulty of all shaping parries against it and, on success, stripping the enemy's shaping weapon from readiness; cannot be used for surprise attacks.
description: The footsteps of the raksha ring loudly in the air. He takes on the aspect of the supreme divine emissary of death; as nothing can stand against him, nothing will. This Charm supplements a Sword or Staff attack, adding the raksha's Essence to the difficulty of all shaping parries against it. If the attack succeeds, the Charm also removes the enemy's shaping weapon from readiness. This Charm cannot be used for surprise attacks.

name: Fearsome Mien
summary: A work of glamour that weaves a terrifying aura after a successful Sword attack, imposing a two-die dice-pool penalty on all Creation-born enemies interacting with the raksha for a scene.
description: The raksha can weave a glamour that terrifies creatures of Creation. This requires a successful Sword attack. This Charm imposes a two-die penalty to the dice pools of all Creation-born enemies interacting with the character. This is a work of glamour, and it has no effect on creatures with Valor + Essence greater than the raksha's highest Sword Ability (Archery, Athletics, Brawl, Melee or Presence).

name: Aegis of a Martial Destiny
summary: The root Charm of World-Devouring Warlord Style, a named sub-tree of Sword Combat Charms telling the story of an emissary of death and fear who rises to cast the world into his shadow: establishes the raksha's motivation for battle early in the story, augmenting a shaping Dodge action with automatic successes equal to her Sword.
description: Early in the story, the raksha establishes her motivation for battle. She cannot use this Charm if she has taken an aggressive shaping action this story. The raksha uses this Charm to augment a shaping Dodge action; this Charm adds her Sword in automatic successes to her Dodge roll.

name: Antagonist-Naming Technique
summary: Defines the raksha and a chosen (existing) antagonist as the principal characters of the story, preventing shaping actions that would remove either of them as active characters -- for example, killing the raksha would have to somehow also bring her back to life.
description: The raksha defines herself and an antagonist of her choice as the principal characters of the story; the antagonist must exist. This Charm prevents the use of shaping actions that remove the raksha or her named antagonist as active characters in the story. For example, no one can use a shaping action to kill the raksha without also in some fashion bringing her back to life.

name: Thematic Stunting Methodology
summary: Defines desirable premises of the story and genre for a full story, adding five extra dice to the raksha's stunt pool.
description: The raksha defines desirable premises of the story and genre. This adds five extra dice to her stunt pool.

name: World-Devouring Warlord Stance
summary: A Stance-type Charm pouring Essence into the raksha's Sword Grace, adding her permanent Essence to initiative, Sword attack pools, Sword defense pools, and the raw pre-soak damage of Sword attacks; only one Stance-type Charm can be active at a time.
description: The raksha pours Essence into her Sword Grace. Flush with the power of the Sword, she becomes a devotee of battle and assumes the stance of an all-devouring warlord. This Charm adds the raksha's permanent Essence to her initiative, her Sword attack pools, her Sword defense pools, and the raw (pre-soak) damage of Sword attacks. This is a Stance-type Charm; characters cannot use more than one Stance-type Charm at a time.
reviewFlags: This is a Stance-type Charm; characters cannot use more than one Stance-type Charm at a time (the same unmodeled mechanic already flagged for Spirit-Twisting Obsession Stance, All-Consuming God-Monster Stance, and Laughing Monster Stance -- no schema field tracks Stance-type exclusivity).

name: Gathering the Crows
summary: Summons a greater host of literal-extra troops to swell the raksha's army, cumulatively increasing the defense quality of her chosen shaping weapon by one per invocation.
description: The raksha summons servants and minions. Each invocation of this Charm calls forth a greater host to support her in war. Most of the troops are literal extras -- they don't ever interact with enemies directly, but they swell the raksha's army ominously. This Charm increases the defense quality of her chosen shaping weapon by one, and multiple invocations of this Charm are cumulative.
prerequisiteText: Transient Work of Flesh and Bone, World-Devouring Warlord Stance

name: Army-Supporting Behemoth Invocation
summary: Summons monsters, horrors and war machines to support the raksha's army, cumulatively increasing the damage of her chosen shaping weapon by one per invocation.
description: The raksha summons monsters, horrors and war machines to serve with his army. Each use of this Charm supports his forces with another great monster or a handful of smaller beasts. This Charm increases the damage of her chosen shaping weapon by one, and multiple invocations of this Charm are cumulative.

name: Avatar of War
summary: Closing her ears to screams and blandishments alike, the raksha marches to war: an immediate full-dice-pool Sword counterattack against any character attacking her with a shaping action, resolved before the original attack's damage is determined.
description: Closing her ears to screams and blandishments alike, the raksha marches to war. This Charm lets her immediately execute a Sword attack at her full dice pool against any character attacking her with a shaping action. This counterattack is resolved after the original attack is rolled but before its damage is determined.
prerequisiteText: Gathering the Crows, Army-Supporting Behemoth Invocation

name: Harmony of Fortune and Hate
summary: Bends hostile weather, ill fortune and unpleasant terrain against the enemy's will to fight, cumulatively increasing the difficulty of defending against the raksha's Sword attacks (up to a maximum equal to her Essence).
description: The pattern of events develops inexorably in the raksha's favor. Hostile weather, strokes of ill fortune and unpleasant terrain eat away at the enemy's will and power to fight. Each use of this Charm increases the difficulty of defense against the raksha's Sword attacks by one; multiple invocations of this Charm stack, up to a maximum increased difficulty equal to the raksha's Essence.

name: Preemptive Declaration of Victory
summary: The capstone of World-Devouring Warlord Style: a Sword attack that converts damage dice directly into successes and, on success, forces all shaped creatures in combat with the raksha to succeed at a Valor roll or surrender in a five-die-penalized rout for the rest of the scene.
description: Crushing her enemy underfoot, the raksha declares victory. The raksha makes a Sword attack; if she succeeds, this Charm converts the damage dice directly into successes. The damage of this attack can affect the creatures of Creation: if the Sword attack succeeds, all shaped creatures directly or indirectly in combat with the character realize themselves defeated, and their players must succeed at a Valor roll or the characters lay down their arms in resigned surrender. For the rest of the scene, the defeated suffer a five-die penalty on all combat actions. This Charm is a work of glamour and has no effect on creatures with Valor + Essence greater than the raksha's highest Sword Ability (Archery, Athletics, Brawl, Melee or Presence).
prerequisiteText: Avatar of War, Harmony of Fortune and Hate

name: Hundred-Hand Style
summary: Attunes the raksha's shape to the harmony of principles so mind and body function as many rather than one, reducing multiple-action penalties by 1 (to a minimum of 0).
description: The raksha attunes her shape to the harmony of principles, so that her mind and body function as many rather than one. This Charm is favored by raksha with extra arms, heads or personalities, but these things are not necessary to receive the Charm's primary benefit. Activating this Charm reduces multiple action penalties by 1, to a minimum of 0.

name: Millipede Mind
summary: Divides control of the raksha's mind and body among her five Graces, reducing multiple-action penalties by 2 (to a minimum of 0); stacks with its own prerequisite, Hundred-Hand Style.
description: The raksha divides control of her mind and body among her Graces, so that five distinct principles guide her every action. Activating this Charm reduces multiple action penalties by 2, to a minimum of 0. The raksha can benefit from this Charm and its prerequisite simultaneously.

name: Grace of the Infinite Revolving Spheres
summary: Lets the raksha flow through the interwoven desires of her five component Graces so that, when splitting her dice pool, her first five actions suffer no multiple-action penalties; stacks with its prerequisites.
description: The raksha flows smoothly through the interwoven desires of his five component Graces. If he splits his dice pool, the first five actions suffer no multiple-action penalties. The raksha can benefit from this Charm and its prerequisites simultaneously.

name: Harmonious Primordial Spirit
summary: Embeds one of the raksha's own Graces in a consenting common raksha, turning it into a bound spiritual-extension servant with heroic-commoner qualities that shares use of the embedded Grace with the original owner.
description: The raksha embeds one of her Graces in a consenting common raksha, replacing his own version of that Grace. The creature becomes a bound subsidiary entity, a spiritual extension of the raksha's body, with the qualities and abilities of a heroic commoner. The servant serves the raksha loyally and at all times knows her will. The activating raksha still has access to the Grace while this Charm is in effect, and the subsidiary raksha also uses this Grace for Charms and damage.

name: Long-Arm Technique
summary: Lets the raksha's limbs unfold like flowing geysers of flesh on attack, extending her reach by two yards per gossamer spent and letting her strike mounted opponents without penalty.
description: Raksha with this Charm are never quite so far from their victims as they might appear. Fair Folk under this Charm's influence look normal until they attack, when their limbs stretch and unfold like flowing geysers of flesh. For each gossamer spent, this Charm adds two yards to the raksha's reach. Raksha with this Charm active can strike opponents on horseback without penalty.

name: Gossamer Wing Flight
summary: Shapes wings from mixed Wyld and Creation substance, letting the raksha fly at normal speed (half speed to ascend, double to dive), though the wings impose a Dexterity penalty while airborne unless the Charm is purchased a second time.
description: The raksha forms wings for himself, shaping them from the mixed substances of the Wyld and Creation. Nobles often build their wings from the appropriate element; commoners base theirs on the wings of birds or insects. The raksha's wingspan is at least equal to his height, and he cannot fly if he cannot spread his wings; he can fly at normal speed, ascend at half speed, or dive at twice his normal speed. Gossamer wings are clumsy, and the character suffers a +2 difficulty penalty on all Dexterity-based normal dice actions while airborne; the player can eliminate this penalty by purchasing this Charm a second time. Raksha using either version of this Charm may make fly-by attacks (see the Exalted Players Guide, p. 201).

name: Hiding the Wyld's Touch
summary: Makes the raksha's body language and manner unnaturally human and familiar, granting two automatic successes on normal Social dice actions, though it does not hide an inhuman appearance -- it only makes others notice the 'person within.'
description: The raksha's body language and manner of expression are unnaturally human and familiar -- the monster moves and speaks like an amalgam of old friends, family and lovers. This Charm gives two automatic successes on normal Social dice actions. If the raksha is also hideously inhuman in appearance or behavior, this Charm does not force others to disregard this fact -- they simply find themselves noticing the 'person within.'

name: Armament of Flesh
summary: A permanent mutation granting understated but potent natural weaponry (fangs, nails or horns) sharp enough to puncture steel, usable with the raksha's normal Brawl or Martial Arts dice pools.
description: The raksha develops understated but potent natural weaponry. Her small fangs, pointed nails or thin elegant horns are sharp enough to puncture steel. This affliction gives the raksha a natural attack with Speed -3, Accuracy +1, Defense -1, Damage +4L and Rate 4; she can use this attack with her normal Brawl or Martial Arts attack dice pools. The raksha can shape more blatant and obvious weaponry if desired -- subtlety is simply the standard.

name: Surpassing Excellence
summary: A permanent mutation adding a two-die specialty (not counted against the raksha's specialty limit) to any one Ability, purchasable up to once per dot of the raksha's Sword.
description: In a place between worlds, the raksha forges herself like a weapon, using the elemental Essence of Creation to empower one of her Abilities. This pox adds a permanent two-die specialty to any one Ability, which does not count against her specialty limit. Raksha can use this Charm to purchase inhumanly keen senses -- for example, a two-die Keen Eyesight specialty on Awareness gives benefits commensurate with the Eye Color pox (see Exalted core, p. 280, or Exalted: The Lunars, p. 212). Players can purchase this Charm up to once per dot of the raksha's Sword.

name: Glorious Hero Form
summary: A permanent mutation binding the raksha to Caturbhuja, the shinma that breaks the borders of the possible and impossible, permanently raising a chosen pair (or single) of Attributes; purchasable up to once per dot of the raksha's Sword.
description: The raksha binds herself to the principle Caturbhuja, the shinma that breaks the borders of the possible and impossible; she transcends even the perfection of the raksha. This affliction permanently increases her Attributes in one of the following ways (chosen at purchase): one dot of Strength and one dot of Stamina; one dot of Intelligence and one dot of Perception; one dot of Charisma and one dot of Appearance; one dot of Dexterity; one dot of Wits; or one dot of Manipulation. Players can purchase this Charm up to once per dot of the raksha's Sword.

name: Racing Dragon Speed
summary: A permanent mutation imbuing the raksha's body with the speed of wind, fire or waves, adding five yards to running speed; unusually purchasable up to once per dot of the raksha's Compassion rather than her Sword.
description: The raksha imbues her body with the speed of the wind, the fire or the waves. This Charm permanently adds five yards to the raksha's running speed. Players can purchase this Charm up to once per dot of the raksha's Compassion.
reviewFlags: This Charm's own repurchase cap is keyed to the raksha's Compassion rating rather than her Sword (unlike every other repurchasable Charm in this section, which caps on Sword), confirmed against the rendered page image -- flagged as a genuine outlier, not a transcription error. No schema field tracks per-Charm repurchase caps of any kind.

name: Root of the Perfected Lotus
summary: A permanent mutation that sinks the raksha into the flows of Creation's Essence, granting her the destiny, spirit and attitude to learn Martial Arts Charms as a Dragon-Blooded.
description: The raksha sinks into the flows of the Essence of Creation, shaping in herself the destiny, spirit and attitude necessary to practice supernatural martial arts. This allows her to learn Martial Arts Charms as a Dragon-Blooded.

name: Imposition of Law
summary: Opens the Heart Grace's Name Charms; lets the raksha declare a single Attribute+Ability+specialty combination (or an unrolled task) as a truth about herself that she cannot fail at, backed by her very identity.
description: The player chooses an Attribute, an Ability and a specialty (or, with Storyteller permission, an otherwise-unrolled task such as 'fertility' or 'attracting the notice of the Realm') when purchasing this Charm. On any normal dice action rolling that Attribute+Ability combination within that specialty, the raksha gets automatic success (a minimum of one success after difficulty and defenses) unless a Charm or stunt actively opposes her; if opposed by a Charm or stunt, this Charm instead grants two bonus successes rather than automatic success. For example, a raksha built around Dexterity + Melee (Swords) still misses an attack if the target reflexively dodges with a Charm after already parrying, because the automatic-success guarantee only holds against undefended actions. A player may purchase this Charm once per dot of the raksha's Heart, choosing a different Attribute/Ability/specialty combination each time.
reviewFlags: First Charm of the Heart Grace tree; Name Charms is a two-Charm section (this Charm plus Bastion of the Self), not a branching tree -- neither cites a prerequisite. The source's own text also describes Name Charms as 'key to the construction of behemoths,' a still-unpromoted Fair Folk mechanic.

name: Bastion of the Self (Grace)
summary: A second Name Charm granting the raksha near-total immunity to one category of harm (physical, mental, social, or damaging) as long as the attacker relies on nothing but mundane dice; any Charm-, stunt-, or shaping-augmented attack instead merely gets harder to land.
description: At purchase, the player picks one of four variants: Bastion of the Self (Cup) protects against normal attacks/effects that weaken the raksha and against Cup-shaping attacks; Bastion of the Self (Ring) protects against undue mental influence and Ring-shaping attacks; Bastion of the Self (Staff) protects against undue social influence and Staff-shaping attacks; Bastion of the Self (Sword) protects against normal damaging attacks and Sword-shaping attacks. Against any attack in the chosen category that uses no Charm, stunt, or shaping action, the raksha is simply immune -- the attack fails outright, letting her walk unharmed through an army of unaugmented spearmen. Against an attack in that category backed by even a one- or two-die stunt, a Charm, or a shaping action, this Charm does not grant immunity; it instead raises the difficulty of hitting the raksha by 2.
reviewFlags: The source's own compatibility line limits this Charm to a single purchase ('Players can purchase this Charm only once'), locking in only one of its four Grace-keyed variants (Cup/Ring/Staff/Sword), but then adds its own hedge that a raksha could 'presumably' learn it again later for a second variant, 'subject to Storyteller ruling' -- a genuine source-text ambiguity, not a transcription gap. No schema field tracks per-Charm repurchase limits of any kind.

name: Spectacular Insanity
summary: The root Charm of the Bedlam-Influencing Charms tree (a tree that, unusually, draws its branches from all five Graces rather than just Heart); converts the raksha's entry into bedlam from a pure debility into a fuel source, paying out Willpower and gossamer instead.
description: The raksha reshapes her Virtues as she passes through the gateway Nirakara, changing how her psyche responds to bedlam. Each time this Charm is active and the raksha enters bedlam, invoking it grants her Willpower and gossamer equal to the rating of whichever Virtue's last channel triggered the bedlam.
reviewFlags: Root of the Bedlam-Influencing Charms tree -- unusually, this tree's four branches (Ambrosial Ascension, Bedlam Masterworks, Driven Madness, Raging Vortex Form) are each gated on a different Grace (Cup/Ring/Staff/Sword respectively) rather than all sharing this root Charm's own Heart gating, confirmed against the tree diagram on p. 157 (PDF 158). This Charm's own effect activates during the Bedlam mechanic, which (like the rest of Bedlam's channel-counting trigger) is session/scene-tracked play-table bookkeeping this app does not model.

name: Ambrosial Ascension
summary: A Cup-gated branch of the Bedlam-Influencing tree: while the raksha is in bedlam, she becomes an irresistibly beatific, terrifyingly beautiful figure that anyone trying to impede or attack her must overcome a Willpower roll just to bring themselves to act against.
description: A raksha who enters bedlam with this Charm active radiates an angelic, beatific aspect -- glorious and unconquerable beauty undiminished by the ravening madness written across her face, making her an object every Creation-born character desires. While the raksha is in bedlam and this Charm is active, any character whose player wishes to impede or attack her must first succeed on a difficulty 2 Willpower roll; this roll need only be made once per turn for any given character, not once per action.

name: Bedlam Masterworks
summary: A Ring-gated branch of the Bedlam-Influencing tree: when the raksha returns from bedlam, she brings back inexplicable mad craftworks -- artifacts containing recoverable gossamer -- as an involuntary side effect of her Ring's self-defining nature.
description: As the raksha's bedlam fades, her player rolls Intelligence + Craft (Glamour); the resulting objects are craftworks of madness inexplicable even to the raksha whose spirit constructed them. Each success on the roll yields one incomprehensible artifact containing a single point of gossamer, which anyone can later shatter or ravish to claim that gossamer.

name: Driven Madness
summary: A Staff-gated branch of the Bedlam-Influencing tree: the raksha shapes herself to the rigor of a binding oath, gaining bonus successes on Virtue rolls that help her keep it -- a benefit that persists even while she is in bedlam.
description: The raksha shapes herself to the rigor of a binding oath. This Charm gives her three bonus successes on all non-shaping Virtue rolls that help her keep that oath, and this bonus continues to apply even while she is in bedlam, when her Virtue rolls would otherwise suffer the standard +2 bedlam difficulty penalty.

name: Raging Vortex Form
summary: A Sword-gated branch of the Bedlam-Influencing tree: bedlam triggers a passage through Nirakara into monstrous shape, letting the raksha temporarily mutate herself with mutation points scaled to half her permanent Willpower for as long as bedlam lasts.
description: At the dry base of the raksha's well of Virtue a monster lurks; bedlam can trigger a passage through Nirakara and the assumption of monstrous shape. Activating this Charm while in bedlam grants the raksha temporary mutation points equal to half her permanent Willpower, which can simulate the permanent effects of any raksha Charms without calcifying her (the normal Essence-plus-mutation-points cap does not force calcification here) and which last only until she leaves bedlam. The player chooses the specific mutations when purchasing the Charm and can only change that choice when the raksha's permanent Willpower rating itself changes.

name: Mad God Mien
summary: A permanent Charm layered onto any active Assumption-type Charm that makes the raksha wholly alien to Creation: raises the cost of all her Assumption-type Charms, hardens her against Charms that twist her body, and makes Creation-born powers treat her as an automaton immune to most direct mental influence -- undoable only by specific fate-binding powers.
description: Some raksha learn to adopt shape while remaining wholly alien to Creation. As they pass through Nirakara and fill themselves with Creation's Essence, they twist it into the raw, mad structures of the Wyld. Learning this Charm permanently increases the cost of all Assumption-type Charms by 2 gossamer or 2 mutation points. This Charm adds 1 to the difficulty of Charms that twist or reshape the raksha's body. It also makes the Charms and powers of the Creation-born treat the raksha as an automaton and a creature outside of fate, immune to most direct mental influence effects; glamour sorcery cast with the permanent version of this Charm is immune to normal sorcerous countermagic. The effects of this Charm are a matter of structure rather than power -- it can be undone by powers that bind the raksha (or spell) into Creation, such as the Greater Sign of Jupiter (Exalted: The Sidereals) or Harmony with Reality Technique (Exalted: The Lunars).
reviewFlags: This Charm's own Prerequisite Charms line reads 'Any Assumption-type Charm' rather than naming a specific Charm, so `prerequisiteCharms` is left empty (per the established superRefine enforcement, which only validates ids that are actually listed) and the real requirement is kept verbatim in `prerequisiteText` instead. extinction-of-desire (Ring Grace tree, promoted in Phase 1c) already references this Charm by name ('gains the benefits of Mad God Mien'); its own stale 'not yet promoted' reviewFlags note was removed now that this row resolves it (that reference remains descriptive narrative text, not a `prerequisiteCharms` dependency, since Extinction of Desire's own gating is entirely different).

name: Sovereign Elemental Shape
summary: The root of the Elemental Influence Charms: lets the raksha reflexively grant a one-die Wyld bonus to a witnessed normal action when the target is defined as drawing on the element the raksha has assumed.
description: The raksha can use the elements of Creation to assist others. This ability affects normal actions rather than shaping actions: Elemental Assistance -- for 1 mote, the raksha can reflexively grant a one-die Wyld bonus to a single witnessed action. The player of the raksha or his target must define how the target uses one of the five elements to assist him, and the raksha must have the Assumption of Elemental Shape for that element active. For example, an archer might gain the assistance of a raksha who has assumed elemental Earth by taking a firm stance and 'rooting herself in the ground.'

name: Element-Weaving Style
summary: Lets the raksha shape an assumed element by touch into complex, intricate forms without tools, via three Craft-based normal-action abilities for air/fire/water, wood, and earth/metal.
description: The raksha can shape the element by touch, rapidly molding it into complex and intricate shapes without tools. These are normal actions rather than shaping actions: Compliant Element Shaping -- for 5 motes, a single Craft roll shapes air, fire or water; sculptures last a single lunar cycle; requires the matching Assumption of Elemental Shape (Air/Fire/Water) active. Compliant Woodland Shaping -- for 5 motes, a single Craft roll shapes wood as if with First Age tools (a -1 difficulty reduction replacing any tool penalty or benefit); requires Assumption of Elemental Shape (Wood) active. Compliant Mountain Shaping -- for 5 motes, a single Craft roll shapes earth and metal as if with First Age tools (same -1 difficulty reduction); requires Assumption of Elemental Shape (Earth) active.

name: Elemental Invocation
summary: The capstone of the Sovereign Elemental Shape line: manifests a treasure of the Wyld in Creation, given shape and form appropriate to the raksha's assumed element, fading away at the end of the story.
description: The raksha manifests in Creation one of the treasures of the Wyld. This Charm lets the raksha invoke a possession in Creation, giving it shape and form appropriate to an element whose Essence the raksha has absorbed through Assumption of Elemental Shape. For example, a raksha of air might summon a lethal hazard as a storm, and a raksha of water might call forth a servant in the shape of a siaka. It fades away again at the end of the story. This Charm can call forth even possessions and servants that cannot normally exist in Creation.
reviewFlags: References the 'Possession' Fair Folk Background/wealth concept (described elsewhere in the book, pp. 131-132) that does not yet have its own inventory row or catalog entry; left as descriptive text only, matching the established precedent for citing a not-yet-inventoried mechanic by name.

name: World-Angering Elemental Mastery
summary: The hostile counterpart to Sovereign Elemental Shape: lets the raksha reflexively impose an environmental penalty equal to her Essence on a witnessed normal action of which she disapproves, using her assumed element.
description: The raksha can use the elements of Creation to hinder others. This ability affects normal actions rather than shaping actions: Elemental Hindrance -- for 5 motes, the raksha can reflexively impose an environmental penalty equal to his Essence on a single witnessed action of which he disapproves. The raksha's player must define how his character uses one of the five elements to impose this penalty, and he must have the Assumption of Elemental Shape appropriate to that element active.

name: Teeth of the World
summary: The capstone of the World-Angering Elemental Mastery line: grants five elemental attack abilities (one per Assumption of Elemental Shape variant) that use normal Dexterity-based dice pools rather than shaping actions, each requiring the matching elemental assumption active.
description: The raksha attacks others with the elements of Creation. These abilities affect normal actions rather than shaping actions: Wind Knives (Air) -- for 5 motes, an undodgeable hail/lightning/wind attack with base lethal damage of twice the raksha's Essence and a normal Dexterity + Archery pool, requiring the target within 1,000 yards and visible. Inciting the Ocean's Hunger (Water) -- for 5 motes, an unblockable attack turning a nearby water source against an enemy within five yards of it, base lethal damage twice the raksha's Essence, Dexterity + Brawl pool, target within 100 yards. Thrashing Dragon Fire Dance (Fire) -- for 5 motes, a normal Dexterity + Archery attack against an enemy within five yards of a significant blaze, base damage twice the raksha's Essence (or, without a blaze, a weaker 2L conjured-flame version for 5 motes), range 100 yards. Leaping Forest (Wood) -- for 5 motes, a normal Dexterity + Brawl attack (trees initiate clinches, small wooden objects leap) against an enemy within five yards of a tree or 30 yards of a small wooden object, base lethal damage twice the raksha's Essence, range 100 yards. World-Shaking Heart (Earth) -- for 5 motes, a normal Dexterity + Brawl attack with base damage twice the raksha's Essence and range 500 yards (does not affect targets more than five yards from the ground); alternately, with one success on a normal Dexterity + Brawl action, the raksha can shake the ground within 30 yards, forcing standers to roll Dexterity + Athletics or fall and dealing the raksha's Essence in dice of lethal damage to structures.

name: Elemental Transformation
summary: A repeatable Charm letting the raksha adopt an alternate animal or elemental shape (designed with 3 mutation points, chosen at purchase), speaking to animals of that type and shapeshifting into it as a work of glamour with a two-die penalty on physical and social actions while transformed.
description: The raksha masters the art of transformation, learning to adopt an alternate shape suited to her elemental Essence. The raksha can purchase this Charm more than once, learning an additional shape each time; if an animal shape is chosen, the raksha can speak to animals of that type whenever this Charm is active. This ability affects normal actions rather than shaping actions: Shapeshift -- for 10 motes and 1 Willpower, the raksha changes to the alternate form chosen at purchase (an animal or elemental body whose special abilities are designed with 3 mutation points -- for example, an eagle form built from Gossamer Wing Flight and keen vision via Surpassing Excellence, or a bear form with Armament of Flesh and the Large pox). This change is a work of glamour; it imposes a two-die penalty on the raksha's physical and social actions and grants the benefits of the mutations without spending actual mutation points. The raksha can still talk in the animal form.

name: Mercurial Shape
summary: Makes the raksha's shape a thing of quicksilver and change, letting her reflexively grant herself a two-die Wyld bonus on a normal action by defining how a mutable form achieves it.
description: The raksha makes his shape a thing of quicksilver and change. This ability affects normal actions rather than shaping actions: Mutable Form -- for 5 motes, the raksha can reflexively give himself a two-die Wyld bonus. The raksha must define how he uses a mutable form to achieve this bonus -- for example, arms that lengthen and retract for a Larceny roll to steal an Exalt's sword, an ever-changing shape for a Survival roll to avoid pursuit, or a light effort of shapeshifting for a Larceny roll to create a disguise.

name: Elegant Muse Attitude
summary: Lets the raksha reflexively grant a one-die Wyld bonus to a witnessed normal action by defining how the target draws on raksha-inspired passion.
description: The raksha can use emotion to assist others. This ability affects normal actions rather than shaping actions: Emotional Assistance -- for 1 mote, the raksha can reflexively grant a one-die Wyld bonus to a single witnessed action. The player of the raksha or his target must define how the target uses raksha-inspired passion to assist himself. The raksha must have Assumption of Dreams and Passion active.

name: Emotion-Weaving Style
summary: Lets the raksha reshape a target's Nature for a story by carving their mind with embedded emotional Essence, an artificial change the target can consciously ignore but finds uncomfortable to resist.
description: The raksha uses the emotional Essence embedded in his alien soul to shape, mold and carve the minds of others. This ability affects normal actions rather than shaping actions: Great Craft of Minds -- the raksha spends 5 motes, and his player rolls Conviction + Performance as a normal action against a difficulty equal to the target's Essence. On a success, the raksha can change the target's Nature to a Nature of the raksha's choice; this change lasts for one story. The change is an artificial and artistic twisting of the target's spirit driven by emotional blocks set up within the target's mind -- targets can ignore its non-mechanical impact but find it uncomfortable to do so.

name: Emotional Invocation
summary: The capstone of the Elegant Muse Attitude line: manifests a treasure of the Wyld in Creation, its shape and Essence filled with the emotion the raksha has assumed, giving it an odd and appealing character to onlookers.
description: The raksha manifests in Creation one of the treasures of the Wyld. This Charm lets the raksha invoke a possession into Creation, filling the gaps in its shape and Essence with the emotion the raksha has assumed via Assumption of Dreams and Passion. For example, a raksha enshrouded in lust could summon a cabinet or a mutated siaka, but both would have an odd and sensual appeal for those who looked upon them.

name: Unwanted Obsession Provocation Technique
summary: The hostile counterpart to Elegant Muse Attitude: lets the raksha reflexively impose an environmental penalty equal to her Essence on a witnessed normal action of which she disapproves, using her assumed emotional mien.
description: The raksha can use the emotional Essence flooding him to drive others to distraction. This ability affects normal actions rather than shaping actions: Emotional Hindrance -- for 5 motes, the raksha can reflexively impose an environmental penalty equal to his Essence on a single witnessed action of which he disapproves. The raksha's player must define how his character uses the emotional mien imposed by Assumption of Dreams and Passion to inflict this penalty.

name: Essence-Disrobing Passion
summary: The capstone of the Unwanted Obsession Provocation Technique line: an unparryable emotional attack that strips motes from a witnessed target and inflicts a stacking one-die penalty on their normal actions for the rest of the scene.
description: The raksha attacks the Essence patterns of others with madly surging dreams. This ability affects normal actions rather than shaping actions: Mote-Scattering Storm -- for 5 motes, the raksha can overwhelm the thoughts and Essence of a witnessed target with unruly emotion. This is a normal action with a Conviction + Performance dice pool and a base difficulty equal to the target's permanent Essence; this attack is intangible and cannot be parried without Charms or stunts capable of deflecting such attacks. If the raksha succeeds, the target loses motes equal to the raksha's Essence and suffers a one-die environmental penalty on normal actions for the rest of the scene. This penalty is cumulative with the penalty for Emotional Hindrance but not with itself.

name: Ravishing the Created Form
summary: The root of the Feeding Charms tree: touches a consenting Creation-born target and rolls a feeding Grace as a Cup-shaping attack to permanently drain Willpower or a Virtue dot, recovering 10 motes of temporary Essence per Trait point drained.
description: Fair Folk in Creation devour the Willpower and Virtues of mortals to live. To use this Charm, a raksha touches a consenting Creation-born target, and her player rolls a feeding Grace as a Cup-shaping attack. Instead of the normal damage, this Charm reduces the target's permanent Willpower or the target's relevant Virtue (the raksha's choice), by up to one dot per success, to a minimum of 0. This does not increase the raksha's own Traits, but lets the raksha recover 10 motes of temporary Essence for each Trait point the target loses. This Charm is a work of glamour. It cannot feed from creatures whose Willpower + Essence exceeds the raksha's Willpower. Raksha cannot drain Exalted Virtues below the minimums imposed by the Great Curse.

name: Soul-Carving Artifice
summary: Extends ravishment into Creation itself, letting the raksha and a consenting target share a daydream vision that functions as a 10-waypoint Middlemarches space, with anything created inside it fading when the Charm ends.
description: The raksha can ravish others in Creation as in the Wyld. Soul-Carving Artifice lets them shape the Virtues of mortals to their needs and allows them to contest with one another in the thin and dreamless air of the Primordials' world. This Charm creates a daydream or vision shared by the raksha and a consenting target, imposing a one-die distraction penalty on normal dice actions for both. The raksha and target can use shaping actions to change the vision as if it were a 10-waypoint space of the Middlemarches of the Wyld. Anything created in this daydream fades entirely when the Charm's effects end. This Charm is a work of glamour and does not affect characters with Wits + Essence greater than the raksha's Performance.

name: Devouring Wings of the Wyld
summary: Grants a winged raksha the Hypnotic Wings ability, which penalizes onlookers' normal actions and lets the raksha permanently devour a Virtue dot from any Creation-born character who botches a Virtue roll while interacting with her.
description: The shifting patterns of the raksha's wings draw in the soul of those who look upon them. This Charm grants an ability affecting normal actions rather than shaping actions. Hypnotic Wings: the raksha must have wings to use this ability. When she spreads them, every character who can see the wings suffers a +1 difficulty on all normal dice actions. If a Creation-born character's player botches a Virtue roll while interacting with a raksha with hypnotic wings spread, the raksha can permanently and reflexively devour one dot of that target's Virtue, gaining 10 motes of Essence. Raksha can purchase functional wings with Gossamer Wing Flight or an artifact; nonfunctional wings are available to any raksha who wishes them. This Charm is a work of glamour, but it affects the raksha rather than the witnesses, so seeing through it has no effect.
reviewFlags: References Gossamer Wing Flight (a Ring Combat Charms tree Charm, already promoted in Phase 1h) only as one of two ways a raksha might acquire functional wings in the first place; this Charm's own prerequisite is Soul-Carving Artifice, not Gossamer Wing Flight, so no `prerequisiteCharms` change is warranted -- the reference is descriptive narrative text only.

name: Heart-Stealing Kiss
summary: A touch-triggered ravishment: after landing a normal Brawl or Martial Arts touch, the raksha feeds as Ravishing the Created Form but gains 2 motes per drained point and the drained Trait heals faster (one dot per day).
description: The raksha ravishes one of the Creation-born by touch. The raksha can only use this Charm after touching the target with a normal dice action, often requiring a Dexterity + Brawl or Dexterity + Martial Arts roll. The raksha then feeds from the target; this Charm functions as Ravishing the Created Form, save that the raksha gains 2 motes per drained Virtue or Willpower point and the drained Virtues or Willpower heal at one dot per day (rather than the normal, slower rate).

name: Extruded Stomach Feeding
summary: Lets the raksha feed as Ravishing the Created Form using any Grace rather than only a feeding Grace, inverting her Essence pattern to drink through a spiritual 'stomach' visible only to spirits, raksha, and Essence-sighted observers.
description: The raksha inverts her Essence pattern and uses a Minor Grace to drink from her target. She typically remains elegant to mortal eyes, but spirits, raksha and characters using effects such as All-Encompassing Sorcerer's Sight can see the raksha's spiritual 'stomach' pour out her mouth and fix its fanged maw to the target's soul. This Charm functions exactly as Ravishing the Created Form, save that the raksha can feed using any Grace.

name: Soul-Consuming Hunger
summary: A Cup-only shaping attack against the target's Essence that, on success, utterly annihilates a consenting target instead of dealing normal damage, recovering 10 motes of Essence per Virtue or Willpower point the target possessed.
description: Gaping wide the four mouths of her Graces, the raksha swallows a consenting target's soul. The raksha's player rolls her character's Cup Grace (and Cup Grace only) as a Cup-shaping attack against a difficulty of the target's Essence. On a success, instead of normal damage, this Charm utterly annihilates the target. The raksha recovers 10 motes of Essence for each Virtue point or Willpower point the target possessed, to the limits of her normal Essence pool. This Charm is a work of glamour; it cannot be used to feed from creatures whose Willpower + Essence exceeds the raksha's permanent Willpower.

name: Banquet of Crumbs
summary: Lets the raksha recover 1 mote of Essence per success by rolling a feeding Grace as a Cup-shaping action after exposure to strong, appropriate emotions -- with no satiety, but at no gossamer cost.
description: The raksha can sup on the ambient Virtue of Creation, though they find no satiety in it. After exposure to strong, appropriate emotions, the raksha can invoke this Charm and roll a feeding Grace as a Cup-shaping action. This Charm recovers 1 mote of the raksha's Essence per success.

name: Oneiromantic Conjuration
summary: Transforms motes into 1 gossamer by using a dreaming mortal's dream as a crucible; requires access to a dreaming mortal to use.
description: The raksha can use a mortal's dream as a crucible, transforming motes into gossamer. The raksha must have access to a dreaming mortal to use this Charm. This Charm creates 1 gossamer.

name: Demesne-Farming Art
summary: The capstone of the Feeding Charms tree: prunes an uncapped Demesne's wild power for gossamer equal to its rating, though a given Demesne only offers gossamer once per story this way.
description: The raksha prunes the wild power of an uncapped Demesne, creating gossamer from the clippings. The raksha must visit an uncapped Demesne to use this technique. This Charm creates gossamer equal to the Demesne's rating. A given Demesne only offers gossamer once per story.

name: Shiftless Untamed Beauty
summary: Makes the raksha's presence addictive to Creation-born characters who fail a Willpower + Temperance roll, granting the raksha a Social bonus success against addicts and drawing them back to her after time apart.
description: The raksha invests herself with the chaotic majesty of the Wyld -- with its beauty, sometimes its nightmarish horror, but always the raw seductive power of the primordial cauldron of dream. This Charm makes the raksha's presence addictive: players of Creation-born characters who interact with her must make a successful Willpower + Temperance roll against difficulty 2 once per scene, or their characters become addicted. The raksha gets one bonus success on normal Social dice actions against those addicted to her. After each full month apart, addicts' players must succeed at a Willpower roll or their characters feel drawn to return; those drawn to return cannot regain Willpower (save through stunts and Charms) until they spend time with the raksha again. Breaking the addiction requires three consecutive successful Willpower rolls. This Charm is a work of glamour and does not affect characters with Temperance + Essence greater than the raksha's Cup.

name: Maddening Summons
summary: Calls an addicted or formerly addicted character back to the raksha's side via a contested Cup-shaping action, inflicting a derangement on current addicts until they return or break their addiction.
description: A Fair One can call addicted or formerly addicted characters to his side. The raksha chooses a target who has spent time addicted to the raksha and invokes this Charm. The raksha's player rolls Conviction + Performance as a Cup-shaping action against a difficulty of the target's Essence. On a success, this Charm fills the dreams of the target with images of the raksha, his location and his desire for the target to return. Current addicts suffer a derangement of the raksha's choice (delusions, mood swings or obsession) until they break their addiction or return to the raksha's side; former addicts notice the dreams but can ignore them without ill effect. This Charm is a work of glamour and does not affect characters with Temperance + Essence greater than the raksha's Performance, nor characters who do not dream or whose dreams are spoken for by some other effect.

name: Compelling Presence
summary: Instantly addicts a target unless he beats a Willpower + Temperance roll against the raksha's Essence, and thereafter forces addicted attackers to spend an extra Willpower point to take hostile action against her.
description: The raksha shapes herself to match her target's personal dreams and nightmares. This Charm instantly addicts the target, as with Shiftless Untamed Beauty, unless the target's player can successfully roll Willpower + Temperance against a difficulty of the raksha's Essence. Further, characters addicted by means of this Charm cannot attack the raksha without spending an extra Willpower point in each turn in which the addict wishes to take hostile action. The raksha can only use this power against a given target once per turn. This Charm is a work of glamour and does not affect characters with Temperance + Essence greater than the raksha's Cup.

name: Whispers Behind the Eyes
summary: The capstone of the Addiction Charms tree: opens a one-way telepathic channel into an addict's mind for the rest of the story, letting the raksha speak to them directly.
description: Those addicted to the Fair Folk sometimes hear strange mad whispers, the patina of Wyld taint on their minds resonating with the raksha's will. The raksha can use this Charm and a Cup-shaping action to open a channel to an addict's mind, through which -- for the rest of the story -- she can speak. This Charm is a work of glamour and does not affect characters with Temperance + Essence greater than the raksha's Performance.

name: Gladdening Visage
summary: One of the two roots of the World-Shaping Charms tree: makes the raksha appear human (if she looks human) or a natural, beneficent little god (if she does not) to observing creatures of Creation.
description: The raksha makes herself more appealing to the creatures of Creation. If she looks essentially human, this Charm makes others identify her as human. If she does not, they recognize her as a natural and beneficent little god. This Charm is a work of glamour and has no effect on creatures with Perception + Essence greater than the raksha's Performance.
reviewFlags: This Charm's own section opens by describing World-Shaping Charms as 'the core Charms for glamour sorcery' (pp. 205-207), a system not yet promoted into any catalog; left as descriptive text only, matching the established precedent for citing a not-yet-inventoried mechanic by name.

name: Adored by All the Worlds
summary: Attracts temporary Allies or Followers dots (up to the raksha's Essence, divided as she chooses) via a Cup-shaping action, weaving a fate of serenity, loyalty, and pleasure.
description: The raksha weaves a fate of serenity, loyalty and pleasure, thereby attracting tangible support in the form of allies and followers. The raksha's player rolls Conviction + Performance as a Cup-shaping action. This Charm gives the raksha one temporary dot of Allies or Followers per success, to a maximum of his Essence; the raksha can divide successes between Allies and Followers as he chooses. He does not choose his specific allies or followers, but they are always appropriate to his situation. This Charm is a work of glamour and cannot attract allies or followers whose Perception + Essence exceeds the raksha's Performance.

name: Abandoned by All Creatures Curse
summary: Distances a target from his supporters, temporarily reducing his Allies, Followers, or Mentor dots (divided as the raksha chooses) by one dot per success on a contested Cup-shaping action.
description: The raksha weaves fates of confusion and dissent, distancing a creature of Creation from his supporters. The raksha interacts with the target, and then her player rolls Conviction + Larceny as a Cup-shaping action. This Charm temporarily reduces the target's Allies, Followers or Mentor by one dot per success, divided among the Backgrounds as the raksha chooses; her supporters drift away -- distracted, occupied, angry, kidnapped or otherwise unable to come to the character's aid. This is a work of glamour; it cannot drive away creatures whose Wits + Essence exceeds the raksha's Stealth. If the target has Wits + Essence exceeding the raksha's Stealth, he can use stunts or Charms to hunt down lost associates and convince them their anger or preoccupation is illusory.

name: Spite-Summoning Malediction
